column46: Hanover Augt 3 / 14 1750 My Dear Lord, I have received both your Letters; and will obey your Commands about you Lieutenant. Colonel; and endeavour to do so, about the Living of St. Olav's for little Hughes. There has happened here a most melancholy Accident. Your friend More Freechappel, has killed poor Schwicheldt, the Elder, in a Duel. Everybody is concerned for Him. I am sure, I have Reason to be so; having lost one of the best Friends, I had, in this Country. The King is extremely concerned for Him. More Freechappel is gone off. The Duel was, immediately, occasioned by Something, that passed at Court, the night before. Schwicheldt was as Honest, and as good natured a Man, as ever was born. I am much obliged to you, for all your kindness in your long Letter - But it is only a Continuance of your Goodness. I hope, I am well with the Earl of Lincoln. The Duchess of Newcastle sends Her best Service to you, and the Duchess of Richmond; to whom I beg mine. I am, Ever Yours Holes Newcastle

Oxon Jan: 31 (80/81). Honoured Sr. The want of some considerable News, since the coming down of Burnyatts has occasioned my silence ever since. But I can~ot omit this opportunity by Alderman Simpson, who brought us the good news of all your welfares, except Mr Stewardsons, of whom the Town of Kendall, as well as his Relac~ons, may find a loss in time. Sr. I am sensible of the good offices you did my Father of late in agreeing & determining the Controversy betwixt him & Mr Ducats. I wish either of us knew how to make you part of requiteall. The said Mr Ducats & your Cousin Philipson of Crook clubbed for a letter to me since ye dissoluc~on of ye Parliamt, wherein they acquainted me that it was probable that they might both see us att Oxon~ when the Parliamt met & hoped wee would make some provision for them. Mr Ducats says he has no business, yet heel find some, if weel find him lodging. I perceive wee are like to be very throng in Colleges as well as elsewhere, insomuch that the Provost has proffered leave of going home (or being absent) to as many as please whether of the foundation or not. So I leave it to you whether you are willing your son should continue with us or not: he shall have convenience if he stay. It is uncertain how long the Parliamt will sit, we hope theyl be more moderate than the last as to some points. The hurry wee shall be in when they meet, & the fluctuateing condition the Nation is in att prsent (with some other reasons) may be a means to prvaile upon me to decline the Proctors place which comes to our house this ensuing year. I thought I should not have been able to avoid it once, sc: when the Provosts Brother (who is 3 or 4 years my Junr, & who was looked upon as ye only competitor) declared to me openly & freely 6 weeks ago that he would have nothing to do with it. But since he says he has been prvail'd upon to seek for it, upon prospect of a moral Philosophy Lectures place (worth 500l~ in 5 years time) which he may possibly get, if the Provost continue Vicechancellour another year, it being att the disposeall of ye Vicechancellour & the 2 Proctors for the time being, the Dean of Christchurch & the Presidents of Magdalen & St Johns, or any 2 of them & the Vicechancellour. which motive is very considerable & might possibly be a means to get a majority of electors for him in ye College, if I should stand it out. I do design therefore (partly to avoid all controversy & animosity, & partly to oblige ye Provost by compliance) to desist, & to desire another Public Lecturers in the Schools, which comes to our house att ye Act & is to continue 2 years being worth near 30l~ p~ an~u~, which may perhaps prove as advantageous as the other which is not infallibly certain: however it will be less prjudiciall to ye body than the Proctors place, which I perceive the Provost is willing his brother should have. Dr Plot is getting Subscriptions for Staffordshire which is almost ready for the Press, I subscribed in ye Holidays, & any one may subscribe yet, he being in Oxon~ att prsent. The Price will be somewhat higher than that of Oxfordshire. Mr Adams of ye In~er Temple was att Oxon~ lately with some Proposealls (relating to ye true meridian Line & measuring all the Counties in England, which Project 2 or 3 more are upon) which I prsume he has sent to you. Besides the Bp of Oxon~s Sermon (preached before ye house of Lords) printed att ye Theater, There's a new Book printing at Moses Pitts cost, entitled A Brief Survey of ye late Troubles or Civil Wars of England (wherein a true account is given of ye Presbyterians) supposed to be wrote by Sr William Dugdale, but he is not willing to own it in this juncture. Twill be out about Easter & is said to be of 14 or 15s price. If you would dispense with your concerns in the Country, I could wish you would make a Member in Parliamt, especially seeing it is to meet att Oxon~. Mr Vicechancellour told Mr Simson he should be glad to see you, & so should Sr Your most obliged Friend & Served Tho: Dixon. My respects to Mr William & all with you. I have sent you by ye Bearer the Bps Sermon, Dr Plots proposealls & Cellars proposealls somewhat of ye same nature with Adams's. This To the Worpfull Daniel Fleming Esq~ att Rydall-hall near Kendall in Westmoreland. Together with a small Bundle.

column46: Oxon~ Feb. 1. (80/1). Sr I received by this bearer Mr Simpson 5s who has been very kind to me hear. I doe not question but that you have heard ere this, what great preparations are made here for the Court. The Vice-Chancelour hath ordered three Colleges for his majesty, the Queen and their attendants scil. Christ-Church, Corpus Christi and Merton. And the rest of the Colleges are or will be so taken up with other noble men, that it will be very hard for any undergraduats or Batchlours to stay in the University; And if any doe stay in my opinion they had better be away, seeing the absent will keep terms (during ye sitting of ye Parliament) as well as the resident, and also they being so few in number that I believe they will have no exercise, nor any opportunity to study, but innumerous temptations to idleness and spending money. So all these things considered I desire you yt you would be pleased to let me come down about Easter, during their sessions. Though I shall be very well contented either to come or to stay according to your pleasure yet I thought fit to acquaint with ye hardships they are like to undergo which stay. So with my duty to your self and my love to my brothers and sisters I rest Sr Your dutiful son Henry Fleming. For Daniel Fleming Esqir at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

March ye 16 (80/81). Honoured Sr: I recd your full & ample lettr by ye Bearer Burnyatts (which made a sufficient compensation for your late omissions) As also 5£ in money for your Sons use, which I shall disburse accordingly, and when it is gone I know where to get more without petitioning ye Parliament. I am afraid wee should not speed so well there, if the King can not prvaile upon them to supply his exigencies. Wee hope you are not so low as you would insinuate, seeing you are pleased to continue your ancient noble Token of 5s. wherewith wee shall answer your expectac~on by drinking his Mates health, the good agreemt of ye King & Parliamt, & your own personal health & p~sperity. The greatest news I have not send you att prsent is, That his Maty arrived att Oxon~ on Monday last about 5 of ye clock, Only ye Town went to meet him (because it is said his Maty did not expect it from ye University) & the Recorder made a Speech to him att his entrance into ye City, They prsented him & ye Queen with each a pair of Gloves. The Vicechancellour & the Doctors waited on him ye next morning att Christchurch, & the Public Orator made a Speech to him in Latin upon his knees, & another in English to ye Queen, which she seemed to be very well pleased with: After which they all kissed their Mates hands & prsented them with rich Bibles. I have subscribed for Dr Plots History of Staffordshire upon your account, & shall take care of it wn it comes out. Sr Wm Dugdales Book (if it be his) is come out. The price is 13s 6d in sheets, & the Title of it is A view of ye late Troubles, It is an exact narrative of matters of fact, & displays the Presbyterians to the life: which I suppose is one Reason why Sr William will not own it in these Times. My Lt of Lincoln has a new Book come out styled Brutum Fulmen, wherein he makes Animadversions upon ye 2 Popes Bulls which excom~unicated Queen Elizabeth & K. Henr: 8. The price is 5 or 6s bound. The Author is expected att or College this week, The Bp of Exeter came last week. I am glad I shall be able to pleasure Sr George Fletchr with my chamber. I am Sr Your Faithful Friend & humble Served Tho: Dixon. This To the Worpfull Daniel Fleming Esq~ att Rydall-hall near Kendall in Westmoreland prsent.

column46: Oxon~ March 17, (80/1). Sr Yours of Feb. 14 I received with 3l~ and two books: and shortly after I received another letter of March 4, by which you acquainted me of ye death of my Grandmother which I was very sorry to hear. And by both I understand that you would rather have me to stay here during ye sitting of the Parliamt then to come down into ye country, which I am very willing to doe, if I can have any study to stay in, which I a little fear, if I be put out of this which I have now, all ye rest being full. On Monday last his Majesty came into Oxon~ with the Queen and took up their lodgings in Xt Church College but this day he goes to Burford too a horse raise, and returns again on Saturday. This with my duty to your self and my love to all my brothers and sisters, is all from Sr Your very dutiful Son Henry Fleming. For Daniel Fleming Esqir at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

Oxon~ April ye 29th (81). Sr Yors dated April ye 6th I recd by ye Post, and am glad to hear of any occasion thats like to draw you into ye South, & that will thereby give us an opportunity of seeing you at Oxon~. I have told the Vicechancellour what great p~bability there is of your visiting him in May, & he was glad to hear of it. I question whether you may not have begun your journey before these Lines can arrive at Rydall: And therefore in your absence I have directed them to Mr William, the business of them being only to acquaint you that the Bearer is one Mr Nicholson, Fellow of our College, & one of the main Supporters of Moses Pitts new Atlas. He has newly finished one Volume of Germany, whither he had an opportunity to travel not long ago. And he is now going to see his Relac~ons att Plumland in Cumberland, & to see how he likes the Vicarage Bromfeild which ye Bp of Carlisle has p~ferr'd to him, but I suppose heel scarce accept of it. When I was in ye North I desired him to look after your Son Harry, so that I need say no more to recom~end him to you & to desire you to show him the civility of ye Country. I fancy heel but make a short stay in ye North. The Bp of Exeter resigned up Charleton before he left Oxon~, which wee have given to ye Provost, instead of Wayhill, which is indisposed of yet. I fancy either Mr Crostwhait or Mr Mill will have it. I refer you to ye Bearer for ye rest, & remain Sr Your obliged Friend & Served Tho: Dixon. Fitzharris is like to be tried this term, notwithstanding his being impeached by ye late house of Com~mons. This To the Worpfull Daniel Fleming Esq~. att Rydall-Hall near Ambleside in Westmoreland prsent Or in his absence to his Son Mr William Fleming. deliver this.

column46: Oxon~ June ye 18./1681. Sr Hoping yt this letter may find you at home and in good health after your long journey; According to your order I send you here a note of my disburstments, which I hope will come to your hands before Rich. Burnyeats come from home. As I remember when you were in Oxon~ you told me of a book you had concerning Philosophy, (but ye name I have forgot), which I desire you would be pleased to send me, and also Walkers Partickles, and his Idioms or Phrases, if you can spare them, they being very good books, and of a great price. We have had here a very great drought which continues still, all ye ground being so burnt up, that ye best will scarce quite ye charge of mowing. The first thing in the note (scil. for doing exercise in ye schools) cost me 20s; 10s of which for ye first day I had of Mr Dixon and Rich. Burnyeats coming before ye second day, I took 10s out of ye 3l~ which you sent me by him. And this next week I must doe more exercise, (called Generals) which will cost me almost 20s, which I shall pay out of my own money till Burnyeats come. So with my duty to your self, and my love to all my brothers and sisters, I rest Sr Your dutiful son Henry Fleming. For Sr Daniel Fleming Knight att Rydal-hall near Kendal These I believe Mr Dixon will send you a note of his disburstments this post.

column46: Most worthy Sr Great favours do oblige to great acknowledgements, you have been abundant to me in ye one, and I should show myself most vilely ungrateful, should I be defective to you in ye other: for when I seriously consider ye ineffable kindnesses you have been pleased to bestow on me, who of all have least merited ire favour; I cannot but att ye same time admire ye vastness of my debt to you, and wthall rapine at mine own inabilities. But since it is not within the limits of my power proportionably to requite ire goodness, be pleased (noble Sr) to accept of my humble thanks, which are ye only requital my small power will permit me to make. I am infinitely indebted to my Cousin Henry, who has shown great kindness and respect to me ever since I came to Oxford. Pray pardon my presumption in giving you this trouble; and call me as I truly am Oxford. July 20th (81) Your most obliged Cousin and humble Served Henry Browham. ffor The Right Worshipful Sr Daniel Fleming living att Rydall nigh Kendall in Westmerland These

column46: Oxon~ July 20. 81. Sr Your letter I received, and was very glad to hear that you got well home. I received of Rich. Burnyeats 3l~, and according to your order I sent you an account how I disbursed the last by the post, which would have come to your hands before Burnyeats had begun his journey, if he had not come before his usual time. My cousin Browhams son is come to our College, and intends to stay. We had an election this last term for Tabiters, at which there were two rejected, and one elected, and there being yet three places void, I believe we shall have another election the next term. So having no news worth trobleing you withal, this with my duty to your self and my love to all my brothers and sisters is all from Sr your dutiful son Henry Fleming. Mr Todd is gone into the country who promised to see you. For Sr Daniel Fleming Knight, at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

Oxon~ July the 29 (81) Honoured Sr. Since the receipt of yors by ye Bearer (as also of 4£ in money & 5s for a Token, which wee had in ye Com~on room) I wrote to you by Mr Tod, who possibly may not arrive with you long before this Bearer: However I was unwilling to omit eithr opportunity. I referred you in my last to Mr Tod for all late occurrences amongst us. Since he left us our Oxford grand Jury (which consisted of persons of Quality, as Knights, Esquires & my Lt Norris's brother) found the Bill aged College (ye Protestant Joiner) att the Assizes, though it was brought in Ignoramus by such Jury Men as Sheriff Bethel empanell'd. It is supposed that Others (who are clapped up of late for carrying on the same treasonable Design) may be brought before an Oxford Jury, seeing they have such large Consciences above. Picaring who was clapped up long ago in ye Castle by Dr Lamphire for speaking some dangerous words aged the Govermt, having no direct evidence aged him was discharged att our Assizes. On Wednesday last I was chosen public Lecturer for our house for the 2 ensuing years, according to what I hinted formerly when I told you of my declining ye Proctors place: & I suppose I shall be Bursar likewise for the ensuing year. Mr Crostwhait has liberty to give up Way-hill att the year end: So that Mr Skeltons Parsonage will be given up before that time, & probably Mr Dentons att Blechington near Oxon~ may fall vacant: which if it do, I suppose Mr Mill will take it, and then I shall have the choice of Mr Skeltons or the liberty to stay till I see what Mr Crostwhait will do about Wayhill which is the much better Living, having no College Rent to pay out of it, & but one church, whereas Sherburne (or Mr Skeltons Living) has 2 churches upon it, & pays near 40£ p~ an~u~ College Rents. I shall desire my Friends advice herein, & yours sooner than any ones. I have given my Father some hints as to these particulars. I design however to do exercise for my Batchler of Divinity's degree the next Term, & to take it before I accept of prfermt, because it will save compounding. I have spoke to one of ye Composers att ye Theater about altering your Title in ye 2d Vol: of ye Atlas, & he tells me that the Catalogue is printed att London, & that None but new Subscribers are to be putt in it, because if any of ye old ones should be in, Some might think he imposed upon ye world in making them believe that there were Two men of ye same Name under different Titles; yet Isle try further if I can prvaile to have it done. However (He says) that in ye last Volume all the Subscribers will be printed in it according to their prsent Dignity & Quality. If it can~ot be done in ye Atlas att prsent, I shall endeavour to have it done in Dr Plots Books. My respects to Mr William, & your Nephew when you see him. I am Sr Your much obliged Friend & humble Servant Tho: Dixon. To The Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight att Rydall-hall. near Kendall in Westmoreland. prsent.

Oxon~ Sept. 4 (81) Honoured Sr. Yors Dated August ye 19 I recd, in which if you had not looked upon an apology as a requisite, att least convenient to be made for your silence; I should not have expected it, considering ye multiplicity of business you have constantly upon you & othr momentous Reasons which I shall not insist on. The business of these lines is to acquaint you that Stephen College (the protestant Joiner) was executed on Wednesday last about 12 of ye Clock according to sentence in a great measure, that is, he was brought out of ye Castle on a Cart to the place of execution which was between 2 Trees in ye castle-hill-yard, close wthin ye wall, & not by ye high way (as usual) In which place (the Rope being about his Neck all ye while) he made a long Speech (I cannot call it a Confession because he did not acknowledge himself guilty of ye Crimes that were laid to his charge & p~v'd aged him) It lasted almost an hour, & was cun~ing worded according to ye opinion of those who got near enough to hear it. It was (they say) some what of ye Jesuits strain, though he declared himself a Protestant of ye Church of England according to its purest reformac~on, that is, from all Superstition & Idolatry, which words he was unable to explain when he was desired to do it by ye Sheriff. He was out of love with ye Com~on prayer & prtended he found no benefit by it, after it had been read twice or thrice to him in ye time of his respit betwixt Sentence & execution, & though Dr Hall of Pembroke gave him ye Sacramt on Aug. 21. & the Bp visited him once, yet he declared a secret love to ye party & complained much of being debarred ye liberty of having Gifted men to cant & pray with him. Whatever animated his zeal he suffered pretty courageously, & went out of ye world (after he had taken leave of & embraced one Enock a kinsman of his of Trinity College) very quietly without ye least hum or acclamac~on. Ketch was very civil to him (thanks to ye 5 Guin~ey's his Relac~ons gave him) permitting him to hang till (in most men's opinion) he was quite dead before he cut him down & quartered him & burnt his bowels. Most of ye company (which seemed to be 2 or 3000) stayed all ye while. Neither his head nor his Quartrs (which were carried to London that night) are to be hung up, his Maty having remitted ye rigour of ye Law in that particular. The Vicechancellour was close by att his execution & so were a great many othr Doctors & abundance of Masters. Wee know not yet whether the Ignoramus men will be tried with us, if they are it is supposed that Bill Vera may be found aged them though they would not find it aged others. I need not tell you that our friend Dr Oats (now degraded by or newesmongrs to Mr Titus) who was one of Colleges best witnesses aged the Kings evidence is forbid the Court & removed out of Whitehall. It is well if his Tongue, which he prtends has saved ye Nation, do not ruin him upon it, if (as Mudyman says) he be a Man that sacrifices all to his passion. I told you in my last that Bletchington was fallen vacant to ye College by the death of Mr Denton, & wee have since given Mr Mill or prsenta~on to it, so that I shall now (as you advise) consider whether I should take Mr Skeltons Living, which is like to be given up shortly, or wait for Mr Crostwhaits giving up Way-hill, which is much better & which he has ye liberty to resign att Midsum~r if he please, or run ye risk of looseing both & being Senior ffellow. I am Sr Your most obliged Friend & Served Tho: Dixon. To The Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight at Ridall-Hall in Westmoreland prsent.

Oxon~ Nov: 6 (81) Honoured Sr. Since the receipt of yors by Burnyatts I have not had much News to send you, which has occasioned my silence thus long. I confess I had an opportunity of writing to you by Mr Fishers brother, but, it happened, that I was very busy then, which made me omit it. But I can~ot wave this, seeing Mr Nicholson the Bearer (who is going to take possession of Mr Sills prebendary, &, if he please, of Turpenhow also) comes close by your door. I need not give you any character of him, or send any news by him, because hes able to furnish you with all occurrences that have happened among us of late. Heel acquaint you with the reasons why I passt by Mr Skeltons Living of late. As also why he may perhaps refuse Turpenhow. Dr Lamphire, our History professor is much troubled with a delirium, so that it is thought his place may be in the disposeall of ye Convocation ever long. I reserve the rest till the return of Burnyatts, who sets out about Thursday or friday next. and remain Sr Your much obliged Servant Tho: Dixon. These To the Right Honourable Sr Daniel Fleming Knight att Rydall-hall in Westmoreland prsent.

Oxon~ Nov: 10 (81) Honoured Sr. Since yors by the Bearer (by whom I received 7l~ for the use of your Son & the old Quantum for an health which wee spent on ye 5th of Nov:) I wrote to you by Mr Nicholson who is come to take possession of Mr Sills prebendary & Turpenhow too wee fear, if you do not dissuade him from it, with the considerac~on of greater things in ye South in due time. I acquainted you by him that I had forgone Sherburne (Mr Skeltons Living) in hopes either of Way-hill at Midsum~er, if Mr Crostwhait give it up then, or of being Senior ffellow, if he do not. The event must show whether I have done well or ill in it. I would act for the best as far as I am able to judge, & my Friends are pleased to advise. I am very well satisfied with my condition att prsent, & would not change it, unless I thought I could mend it, which possibly may be difficult to do. I remember what the Justice of Stainbankgreen wrote to me sometime after he was possessed of the estate & a good wife, sc: you are well if you know when you are well , which words (coming from a plain down-right honest Man) may perhaps have more in them than wee are aware. However theyl require considerac~on, & accordingly I have done it in wavering the above menc~on'd Vicarage. I think I told you in my last that Dr Lamphire Principal of Hart-hall was much indisposed & crazy in his head, & his distemper continues upon him still, so that several are menc~on'd both for the History professors place (which is worth an 120 or 140l~ p~ an~u~ besides a considerable fine) & the Hall. The latter is in ye disposeall of the Chancellor & the former of ye Convocation. Wee are like to have an election this Term both for ffellows & Tabiters. I can~ot foresee how things will go yet, your Son has 4 Seniors (if the Chancellors Son of Carlisle who is clark of ye College stand) & I know not what number wee shall pitch upon yet, I wish you would hasten Mr Nicholson up: he might help att a dead lift. I am Sr Your faithful Friend & humble Served Tho: Dixon. These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight: att Ridall-hall in Westmoreland prsent

column46: Oxford. November. 10th (81) Worthy Sr When I seriously consider ire unspeakable kindness to me and compare ire goodness with my unworthiness, I cannot but infinitely admire my engagements to you, and with all rapine at mine own inability of making requital: therefore give my pen leave (Most Noble Sr) to return you what I can, my heartiest thanks for all ye fresh tokens of ire love, in particular for ye last; besides ye obligac~on of which, you were pleased to confer the happiness and honour upon me of reading ire lines; which I did never so much as expect to aspire to, knowing how much it was below ye greatness of ire person to take such a trouble upon you, and how little I have merited such a favour at ire hands. My humble duty to you, craving ire pardon for this scrible, and desiring you to doe me the right as to think me Ire most Dutiful Godson Hen: Browham ffor The right Worshipful Sr Daniel Fleming att Rydall nigh Kendall in Westmrland These

column46: Oxon~ Novem. 10. 81. Sr Yours of October. 6. 81 with 3l~ and two books and Cloth for Suit and studying gown I received which will doe very well. I believe we shall have an election for tabiters betwixt this and Christmas, but how things will be carried at it I doe not know. We have been lately afraid of looseing Mr. Dixon, for ye last week Mr Skeleton resigned up his parsonage which Mr Dixon had some thoughts of taking, but having refused it Mr Simpson his im~ediate junr hath taken it. On Monday last Mr Nicholson went towards Carlisle, the Bishop their having sent for him to make him prebend, and to give him a parsonage called Terpenne in Cumberland. So having no news worth writing, with my duty to your self and my love to all my brothers and sisters I rest Sr Your very dutiful son Henry Fleming. For The right worshipful Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

Oxon~ 10ber the 4th (81). Honoured Sr. Having had an Election yesterday both for Fellows & Tabiters, I think my self obliged to let you understand how things went, though the latter did not descend so low as your Son: I spoke to Mr Provost in behalf of him, but he said he was afraid (considering what Seniors we had, & how many Tabiters wee had already, & how many Fellows were like to be taken in) wee could not stretch for him att prsent, but he has p~miss'd to do him a kindness as soon as possible; sc: when the first Tabiter goes of, which will be att Act next p~bably, or att Michaelmas att furthest. Wee elected 2 Tabiters, sc. Jackson & Heartily & left one Highmore (who is 2 or 3 terms your Sons Senior) unelected before him. So that if he continue to appear att the next election wee shall make up 9 Tabiters rather than your Son shall stay behind or lose any time. I am sure the provost will do it. ffour Masters sc. Mr Scot, Mr Clark (who I wish may deserve it) Mr Addison & Mr Smith were elected Fellows, & are to be admitted on St Tho: day. Mr. Nicholson is not returned as yet out of your parts. If he take Turpenhow, he is not like to have the same liberty with Mr Crostwhait of giving it up at ye year end. I recd a lettr lately (which I showed ye Provost) from Rich: Ducats, wherein he acquaints us that there's 193l~ decreed aged Anthony Saul & Robed Gibson of Heversham for our college, & that since the Decree there's 6l~. 13s. 4d for 7 or 8 years accrueing in Mr Wilsons hand. Mr Provost said he had wrote to you about some such thing. I know not what to make of it though I am Bursar. Dr Lamphire of Hart-hall is somewhat recovered of his distemper. I am Sr Your much obliged Servant Tho: Dixon. My respects to Mr William These To the Right Honourable Sr Daniel Fleming Knight att Rydall-hall near Kendall in Westmorland prsent.

Oxon~ Jan. ye 22 (81/82). Honoured Sr. I hope it is not too late to wish you an happy New-year, & to acquaint you that yors bearing date Dec: 9 & 10th came to my hands on Dec: 24th. I have been the longer in returning an Answer, because Mr Vicechancellour was out of Town in ye Holidays, & I was willing to let him know (before I wrote) how careful you had been in manageing ye College concerns in relac~on to Heversham exhibitions, and he is infinitely pleased with what you have done therein, & is thankful to you for your good endeavours to serve ye College upon all occasions. I fancy your Cousin Nicholson will have much ado to p~cure your pardon for his not calling upon in his return to Oxon~, seeing he came through Rydall, He misst my Fathers house likewise, & posted on (att ye rate of an Oxford Hackney) to Kendall that night in hopes to meet a fellow-traveller, who failed him when all was done, & wee think he was right served. It seems he took Instituc~on into Turpenhow as well as ye Prebendary before he left ye North, So that you are like to have him among you again ever long. I perceive wee shall not be able to hinder him from entering upon his year of Grace very shortly: One would think there were a niece in ye case, he is so hasty. Hes gone to Exeter att prsent with the Bps Son, whom Mr Provost sent home for fear of ye worst, he having expressed some good liking to a young Gentlewoman (with in 12 miles of Oxon~) with whom he happened to converse in ye Christmas Holidays. I suppose the young man will scarce return this half year, if at all, But Mr Nicholson will be back wthin a fortnight: Mr Mill, who took his Drs degree since he had Bletchington, is att London. Dr Plots Staffordshire is not like to be published these 2 months yet as far as I can perceive: when it comes out weel endeavour to fulfil your orders. It is well if the second Volume of Germany come out before the Author setle amongst you. Mr Tully of or house who is upon his year of Grace, & who was lately with the ArchBp of York, has left his Grace, intending to live with an Oxford Gentlewoman (whose name was Wit) having been married to her above a Quarter of a year ago. He has got 3 prebendary's (2 in York, & 1 att Rippon) of ye Arch Bp, during his short abode with him: but he wants a parsonage yet. I need not tell you that my Lt Preston is to go to Ambassador into France, or that his brothr Mr Graham of Ch: Church is preferred by him lately to a parsonage in your Country, or upon the edge of Cumberland) vacant by ye death of Mr Usher Senr. My respects to Mr William. I am Sr Your much obliged Friend & Servant Tho: Dixon. Pray prsent my duty to my Father when you see him & my respects to Justice Fisher, acquainting them, if you please, that I shall write to them both shortly. These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight att Rydall-hall near Kendall in Westmoreland

column46: Oxon~ Feb. 11. 81/2. Sr Yours of Jan. ye 25 I received, and according to your order I acquainted Mr Todd with that you mentioned in your letter, and he promised to satisfy you in it as well and as shortly as he can. We have here no news as yet of a Parliament but it is supposed that when there is one, it will be at Oxford. I have enclosed a note of my disburstments, wherein perhaps you may think some things dear, yet I am certain yt I have had every thing now as cheap, and many cheaper, then formerly I have had, when left upon the score. So having no news to acquaint you with, but that all your friends here are well, with my duty to your self, and my love to all my brothers and Sisters I rest Sr Your very dutiful son Henry Fleming. For The Right Worshipful Sr Daniel Fleming Knight at Rydal-hall near Kendal These

Oxon~ March ye 6 (81/82) Honoured Sr. Yors dated Feb: the 18th I recd, by Sr Fisher, who arrived safely with us, & is now fallen to his old trade of Rendering, which will hold him tug for one 2 or 3 years. The slavery is not so great, but that there will be always some found who will be willing to undergo it, so long as it qualifies men for prebends & good Livings. Your Cousin Nicholson has time to consider of Turpenhow till Lady Day, att which time he must declare whether heel stick by it, or his ffellowship. The Bp makes new offers and p~misses to him which I fancy will obleige him to quit his great privileges belonging to a ffellow, & enter upon his year of Grace att Lady Day, which may prove somewhat ominous. He is like to have Father Graham for his neighbour, his Brother (the Lt Preston) having bestowed upon him a good parsonage (which Mr Usher had) upon ye Borders, which he has either taken possession of already, or is coming down to do it. Mr Ward, who was out of his ffellowship att St Tho: day last, is lately married to one Ayleworth's daughter (a chandler in Oxon~) with whom I am afraid he has got no great matter. It is generally observed that our Oxford matches are but indifferent, & his Living being so too, heel have grow rich in hast. I can~ot learn as yet when Dr Plots Staffordshire is like to come abroad. Dr Busby's old proposals about a Catechetick Lecture are on foot again, & it is supposed theyl take in Congregation & Convocation: the Stipend is 80l~ p~ an~u~ for 20 Lectures. His Maty is like to be att Newmarket & Windsor till October. It is said his Royal Hness is to meet ye King att Newmarket. I am Sr Your faithful Servant Tho: Dixon. These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight: att Rydall-hall near Kendall in Westmoreland. prsent.

Oxon~ April ye 6 (82) Honoured Sr: In answer to yors by Sr Fisher I wrote by Mr Simpson of Kendall on March ye 6th: Since which time I received one from you by ye Bearer (His Excellence the Northern Ambassador, who makes as much noise in our parts, as his Brother the Emperor of Fez & Morocco dos elsewhere) as also five pounds in money for the use of your Son & 5s as a Token, wherewith as many of ye company as were att home drunk your health one friday night, when I treated them with cold Capon & chine that were sent to me as presents being Bursar. My brother Bursar, our proctor, has got the Moral philosophy Lecturers place, which as I told you formerly will be worth an 200l~ p~ an~u~ to him for five years, if he continue so long in ye University, & have no cura Animaru~ upon him. His being Senior Proctor & his brother the Vice-chancellour secured it to him. I am to read as often as he for 25l~ p~ an~u~ for 2 years. If Way-hill be given up att Midsum~er & I accept of it, mine will hold as long as my year of Grace. Mr Nicholson has time given by ye College of considering till Whitsuntide what heel do about Turpenhow, & if he stick to it then, his year of Grace is to com~ence from Lady day last past. Dr Busbies Catechetick Lecture is referred to Delegates of Convocation (in number 27) who are to adjust matters & difficulties about it & to report them to ye Convocation in order to their approveing or not approveing of the Amendments, it is thought theyl hardly qualify it so as to make it pass. Your Son had some fits of ye Ague a little while ago, but they are over God be thanked. The money you sent for his use will overdo at present: you shall know how things stand with us before the next return of ye Bearer. I am Sr Your much obliged Friend & humble Servant Tho: Dixon. These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight att Rydall-hall in Westmoreland. prsent.

column46: Oxon~ May 21 -82. Sr Having so fit an opportunity I could not willingly let it pass without troubleing you with a line. I have had the ague again since the last time I write to you, but it did not trouble me long till I got it cured. I suppose we shall have an election for Tabiters the next term, but how many will be elected (whether one or two) it is not yett known, if two I shall then know my fate, having but one Senior and being myself sanding already for Batchlour of Arts. These cloths which I have being almost worn, I mut desire you that you would be pleased to send me cloth for a suite the first opportunity. So with my duty to your self and my love to all my brothers and sisters I rest Sr Your very dutiful son Henry Fleming. For The Right worshipful Sr Daniel Fleming Knight att Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

Oxon~ May ye 21 (82) Honoured Sr. Having not wrote to you since the return of Burnyatts, I am afraid you'll think me negligent. If I had had time I would have wrote to you by Mr Nicholson of our house, who, upon ye Bps request came down into ye North about a month ago, & is since returned. He was at ye Synod & Visitac~on in Carlisle, but came no nearer you than Kendall, where he forgot to leave a lettr for my fathr either in his going down or coming up. I fancy heel give up ye Vicarage (& consequently the Niece) when ell's done, & stick only to ye Prebend (with ye Bps good leave) & his ffellowship, wherewith I perceive the Chancellors place is likewise consistent, if he can catch it. The College will expect to know what heel do att Whitsuntide, as also what Mr Crostwhait will do att Midsum~er. Dr Plots Staffordshire is not like to come out for some time yet. Dr Busby's Catechetick Lecture dos not come to any thing as yet, though it has been twice canva'sst in Convocation, several of the Authors proposealls were rejected & new ones agreed to in their place; yet there are several heads undetermined, which the young Mastrs & the Grave Don~s could not agree upon, & it is questioned whether theyl come to any resoluc~on in the point. Your Son has had some fits of ye Ague since Burnyatts left us, but he is quite rid of them now, God be thanked. I am Sr Your faithful Friend & Served Tho: Dixon. These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight att Rydall-hall near Kendall in Westmoreland. prsent.

Oxon~ June ye 1st (82) Honoured Sr. I wrote to you about 10 days ago by Mr Simson of Kendall, and the Morocco Ambassador having been with us lately, I think myself obliged to give you some account thereof. He came from Windsor on the 30th of May, and (being invited) called in at Sr Timothy Tyrrills att Shotover where he stayed about an hour, & where Dr Hide of our house & public Library Keeper, (who sent him our Liturgy in Arabic to London & has held correspondence with him in his own Language by lettrs) met him in a coach & sat next to him on one hand att ye Table: Att his coming out of Sr Timothys grounds, he was met by above an 100 horse out of Oxon~ on Shotover hill, all which were led up in order & marshalled by one Capt Woods, (an experienced Soldier in ye late Wars & now Butler of Christ Church) next to whom Dr Yerbury of Magdalens (who made a short Speech in English to his Excellence) came up, & the rest in order (being most of them Gentlemen Com~oners, Noblemen & Mastrs of Arts). They brought him into ye City a little before 8 of ye clock att night, he was attended likewise by 4 or 5 coaches. The Streets & Windows were as much crowded as when his Maty came to Town, if not more, They hum~'d him as he came up the Street, & afterwards when he looked out of ye Dining Room in ye Angel from whence he seemed to behold the Scholars & great numbers of people in the streets with great satisfaction, laughing att them heartily. Shortly after his arriveall att ye Angel the Vicechancellour & Drs waited on him, & Mr Wyatt (the Univrsity orator) made a short speech to him in Latin, the substance of which being interpreted to him he prsently made a reply to this effect, That upon his Maty's invitac~on he was come to see the Univrsity, & that he was sensible how loyal they were or else he would not have visited them, & that he thank them for their civilities & would acquaint his Maty therewith. The next morning he sent word to the Vicechancellour that he would give him a visit, which he accordingly did about 8 of ye clock: Wee had ye great Gates open for him & made a lane betwixt them & the chapel which he passed through, & viewed first the chapel, then Sr Josephs Buildings, and then the Hall, where the Horn was prsented to him full of Ale, wherein they drunk his health, but he refused to drink himself, jesting in his own country language & proverb, God deliver him from Horns . From our College he went down to the Physic Garden, & viewed Magdalen College, then New College, then Within, then St Johns and Trinity and some other Colleges all before Din~er. After din~er about 4 of ye clock (the Convocation Bell having done att three) he came to the Theater, which, in my opinion, was fuller of Scholars, Strangers & Ladies than att Act, where he was entertained first with Wind Music in ye Stairs (as the Prince of Orange was before him long ago) then with a long Speech in Latin by ye Orator, after which the Proctor read his Matys Letter to ye Convocation, wherein he desired the Univrsity to show him all the respect imaginable. Then a Copy of Verses (in ye Com~endac~on of Africa) were spoken by one Mordant Student of Ch: Church & brothr to the Lt Mordant: after which he was entertained with Music both Vocal & Instrumental, & then that Solemnity ended: He was placed in ye Vicechancellrs Seat or rather equal to it, His Interpreter (who is an English Renegade & had his pardon granted him before he durst come over) standing by him. There were several of his Retinue in their uncouth Garbs & Turbans not far from him. From ye Theater he went to ye Convocation house & Divinity School & so to the Library, where Dr Hide aforemenc~ond made a Speech to him in Arabic (or in his own Language) with which he was hugely pleased, as also with the Arabic Books which he showed him afterwards. From the Library he went to see several Colleges & particularly Christ Church, where the Bp gave him a collation. He went out this morning about 7 of ye clock, and is to dine (as it is said) with my Lt Norris at Rycaut. The Univrsity gave him no Treat (because his Maty was aged it) but they prsented him with 5 Arabic Books & the Cuts of ye Colleges all richly bound, the names of 3 of ye Books were Avicen's philosophy, Euclids Elements & the Nubian Geography: They cost 20s a peace binding. He seemed so well pleased with them and with the Civilities shown him, that he p~missd Dr Hide that, if there were any Books in all Africa which the Univrsity wanted & had a mind to have, he would do his utmost to procure them for them. So the Dr has given him the names of some Books, which it is thought heel send: He being a man of great integrity & very religious, having prayers 5 times a day and night together. He has a Melancholy thoughtful look, & is not so Tawny as the rest by much, he wears a thin kind of Turban on his head, & a kind of Slippers on his feet, being bare legged, & having rich Lin~en or a loose Garmt rolled about his Body; he has a stately gate (though he was in his Coach all but in ye Colleges) & seems to be somewhat above 30 years of age. He eats no flesh but very much parched & of his own Cooks dressing, his usual Liquor is milk & water, So that if he knew of his Interpreters being drunk with wine (on ye 30th, as they say he was & fell of his horse) it would go near to cost him head. He expresses a huge esteem & veneration for his Maty upon all occasions, & they say the King & the Duke have a very great respect for him. I am afraid I have been too tedious & therefore crave leave to remain Sr Your much obliged Served: Tho: Dixon. These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight att Rydall-hall near Kendall in Westmoreland

Oxon~ June ye 18 (82) Honoured Sr In my last on June ye 1st. I gave you an account of the entertainmt of the Morocco Ambassador att Oxon~, which, I prsume, you have since received in print in ye Gazett. The business of these Lines is to give you an account of Way-hill, which Mr Crostwhait has thought fit to part with & resign to the great admirac~on both of ye College & the University & some say of the Bp of Oxon~ likewise, who it seems was heard to say att the Visitac~on att Bestir this week, that if one of his house should have done so, he would have turned him out im~ediately. The Provost, upon his giving of it up, desired me to carry him to ye Tavern & give him as much wine as he could drink, that he might say he was not himself when he did it: Several other Remarks have been made upon it both by him & others. So that I am in a man~er necessitaten to take it to avoid such imputac~ons & reflections. I confess I could have been as well content, if he had kept it, but seeing he did not, it would seem neither wisdom (nor perhaps policy) in me to forego it: And upon these considerac~ons, as also upon the advice of very good friends, I made my application to the company for it, & they have unanimously given it to me (as also a year of Grace ending att the last of July come a twelve month) & I have accordingly treated for it: & shall be obliged, I am afraid, (to prevent damages & inconveniences that may arise from Sequestrac~ons & the neglect of letting it, the harvest being att hand) to take Instituc~on & Induction sooner than I designed. Isle get an election for Tabiters if I can before I lose my vote. However Isle do my utmost in hastening of it upon your Sons account, who I know is as sure of it as if he had it. I have spoken to the Provost already & he has p~miss'd to be mindful of him & I know the fellows, att least a majority of them (but I fancy all) will be ready to befriend him. So that I do not doubt but he is as sure of it as I am of Way-hill, The profits whereof come in partly by Glebe & Tithes, & partly by a Fair, which in 2 days (every Michaelmas) brings in 50 or 60l~. All which the Provost let for 215l~ that year he had it. I question whether it may be set for so much again, yet I fancy it will prove as good as a double ffellowship. The worst thing belonging to it is a bad house, which I may possibly rebuild in time as my Revenues come in, & so make some returns of gratitude to the College. I have not time to send you the particulars of your Sons accounts att prsent, because I am employed about my Latin Sermon, which I am to preach for my Batchler of Divinity's degree: which I design to take before Instituc~on & Induction to prevent charges of compounding in the University where I think of staying till my year of Grace be out, & where I could have lived contentedly if my senior had thought fit to march of, & had not thrown such a great temptac~on in my way. It would look like too great a peace of self-denyall to forgo it, & I hope by accepting of it both to answer the design of the Founder, & to discharge a good Conscience, which will be more satisfactory than any thing perhaps I could oppose to my self in renounceing of it. Wee must not all expect to be Vice-chancellours, & it is hazardous waiting for dead men's shoes. I am Sr Your humble Served Th: Dixon. These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight at Rydall-hall in Westmoreland.

column46: Oxford. July. 26th 82. Honoured Sr I would make an apology for this my second presumption, but that I think I should be much awanting to my self, if I did not sometimes kiss your hand with a letter, not only to discharge my duty, but also to make my grateful and humble acknowledgemts for the many, fresh and signal tokens of your love. But if for all this, this paper be resented as a trouble by you, I must beg pardon of that same goodness, which induced me hereunto, when I considered that you were pleased to descend so low, as by ire last kindness to remember me the most unworthy of all those that rest obliged to you. Pray tender my humble service to all my Cousins; and though I could never aspire to that honour and happiness as to be acquainted with any one of them; yet give me leave to tell them, they have an unknown friend, whose life and fortunes are totally devoted to all their services. After my humble duty to you, give me leave to subscribe my self, Ire most obedient Godson & Obliged Servant Hen: Browham For The right worshipful Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal in Westmorland. These

Oxon~ July ye 27 (82) Honoured Sr. Since yors by the Bearer (by whom I recd 4l~ in money for your Sons use & 5s for a Token which those shall partake of who can befriend your Son) I wrote to you by my brother James: & received one from you by the post on July ye 12th, which bore date July ye 1st : in which I am sensible how real a well-wisher you are to me, & have ever since been the better pleased with my choice of Way-hill, because you approve of it. I have not been able to prvail for an election of Tabiters this Term. The Provost being full of business, & being likewise willing to observe the old Rule of having as many elections att the same time as may be. So that I do not doubt but the next Term will p~duce some Tabiters as well as a ffellow & a chaplain: your Son must have patience in the mean time, & weell make what p~gress wee can in our Studdy's, especially in philosophy & ye Mathematics which he has a fancy for. I am so full of College Accounts att prsent (being to end all my years concerns as Bursar this week) that I must beg your excuse for any other: I hope I shall make good my p~miss as to your Sons, before the next return of ye Bearer. Wee are like to have a new Vicechancellour shortly, the Chancellors Letter being already come for Dr Marshall, Rector of Lincoln & Dean of Gloucester. Our City, having much of the leaven of ye Great City in it, is served with a Quo Warranto lately as well as it. It may possibly be as ill to digest as an Abhorrence, which with much ado was lately set on foot & finished. It is scarce got to London yett. The 2 Terraefilij were very smart one upon another, but one of them is like to cry peccavi for lashing Dr Busby. Mr Nicholson is come into your parts again, I hope heel not pass by again without calling. Hes come for an Arch Deaconry or Chancellors place now, so that heel scarce (or rathr must not) part with ye Niece. My service to Mr William I am Sr Your most obliged Friend & Servant Tho: Dixon. These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight att Ridall-Hall. in Westmoreland. prsent.

column46: Oxon~ July ye 27. 82. Sr Yours of Jun. ye 14 and June ye 21 I have received with cloth &c for a suit and 3l~ - 2s - 6d of which (according to your order) I gave to my cousin Browham 2s - 6d. I have sent by this bearer Rich. Burnyeate, Walker's education of young Gentlemen, which cost 2s. And I have also sent an account of my disburstments, which I hope will satisfy you well. I have been at several booksellers shops, to know ye price of Humph. Prideaux's Marble Oxoniensia, and they tell me that ye best is sold for 15s. My uncle Dalston was here lately and has entered his eldest son com~oner of our College. So having no news worth writing, with my duty to your self, and my love to all my brothers and sisters I remain Your dutiful son Henry Fleming. For The Right worshipful Sr Daniel Fleming Knight at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

column46: Oxon~ Septem. 16. 82. Sr Although I have not heard from you this long time, I hope you are all well, as we are here. We shall have an election for Tabitors without question the next term, but whether Mr Provost will be pleased to have one or two elected is not yett certainly known: if two I shall then (being the second Senior) know my fate. It will be something chargeable if I be elected, both at ye election, and after for taking my degree; So that I hope you will be pleased to send with Rich. Burnyeats money something more than usual least I should then be too much in my Tutors books. We have no news here worth writing, so with my duty to your self, and my love to all my Brothers and Sisters I remain Your very dutiful son Henry Fleming. For The right worshipful Sr Daniel Fleming Knight at Rydal-hall near Kendal These

Oxon~ Oct: ye 8 (82) Honoured Sr. Since mine by Burnyatts July ye 27th my new prefermt has involved me in a peck of troubles, which have made me longer silent than I would (or ought to have been) I know not whether you have heard of it or not, but the Corporac~on of Andover (wthin 3 miles of Weyhill) have surrendered their charter lately & have (by a surprise) got a clause in their new one, which is like to spoil my share in ye Fair, as also Mr Drakes, who is chief Farmer to ye Hospital of Ewelme under Dr Luff the Regius Professor of Physic in Oxon~. They designed to have ye whole p~fitts of ye late Fair at Michaelmas, but upon a petition of ye Vicechancellors to his Maty in the behalf of ye Univrsity & College, they were forced to be content with their ancient Quantum: However wee are to have a Hearing before ye King & Council on ye 3d of ye next month, but it is thought theyl not stand to their determinac~on, but will desire an appeal to ye Com~on Law, where, they are told, they shall have the better: Our right & title is grounded upon prscription, & theirs on their new grant, though indeed the Fair was held att Weyhill by ye late charter ye 41st of Eliz: yet wee can p~ve a Fair there 70 or 80 years before that. However since that time they have enjoyed ye p~fitts of weights & scales & othr dues, & the Rector & ye Tenants of Ewelme Hospital the p~fitts of ye Booths & Sheeppens. So that wee reckon our plea is good, however wee may come of. If ye business should be traversed to ye Com~on Law or Chancery, I see no reason that I should be at ye expense of ye suit, though ye College may possibly expect it, If they should, & be unwilling to continue me in my fellowship till it be decided, I am thinking of desiring to return to my fellowship & leaving ye Living (which is about 140l~ p~ an~u~ with out ye Fair) to some other to manage ye controvrsy, if you approve hereof. Wee shall better see what to think of things about a month hence: In ye interim all I have to add is That Dr Floyd, principal of Jesus, came in ViceChancellour on ye 6th instant, & that 3 or 4l~ will be sufficient for your Sons use by Burnyatts. I am Sr Yors Tho: Dixon. These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight att Rydall-hall. in Westmoreland. prsent. To be sent by ye Post to Lancaster & so to Kendall. Post pt to London 2d. 3

Oxon~ Oct: ye 23 (82) Honoured Sr Since mine by ye Post on ye 8th instant (wherein I gave you a short account of the new & unexpected difficulties & troubles that were like to arise touching Wayhill Fair) I received one from you on ye 21st instant att my return from London, (from whence I brought the enclosed, &) whither I (as also ye Provost) am like to return again wthin these 10 days, The business of Wayhill Fair being to come before ye King & Council on ye 3d of Nov: next: If it go any further Isle see what the College will do, and if theyl do nothing, Isle see what is best for me to do. I have been so hurried about of late that I am forced to run upon ye score with you for your sons Accounts, but I hope to give a faithful Narrative thereof ever long, att least att his advancemt into an higher Sphere which (I hope) will not be long deferred now. Wee expect Mr Nicholson this week, It seems he has got the ArchDeaconry of Carlisle, and wee expect to hear of some appurtenances or encumbrances (or Nepotismo's) being an~ext to it. The convenience of ye Bearer (my namesake) was an inducemt to write to you att prsent. I hope to write to you more fully att Burnyatt's return, if I am in Town then. On ye 6th instant Dr Floyd (principal of Jesus College) succeed or provost in his Vicechancellourship. Our city of Oxon~ is gone up to London to defend their charter (as well as they are able) aged ye Quo Warranto. I did not care if Andover had one aged their new one. My service to Mr William. I am Sr Your much obliged Friend & humble Servant Tho: Dixon. These. To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight at Rydall-Hall near Kendall in Westmoreland. prsent

column46: Oxon~ November. 9.82. Sr Yours by the bearer with 3l~ I have received, and according to your order, I gave your letter to Mr Todd, and would also have payed him for the book he sent you, but he would not take anything for it, only desiering me to acquaint you when I write that he was very glad that you were pleased to accept of so small a present. Mr Dixon has been at London almost two weeks and is not yett come home, so that you cannot have any account now from him. I shall shortly acquaint you how things are carried at the election the time being now very near. So having no news worth writing, hoping that all are well with you, with my duty to yourself, and my love to all my brothers and sisters, I ever remain Sr Your very dutiful son Henry Fleming. For The Right worshipful Sr Daniel Fleming Knight at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

London Nov: ye 11 (82) Honoured Sr. In my last by a young man of our College, I acquainted you that I thought I should see London shortly, & I have accordingly done it twice of late, & have continued in Town (this latter time) a fortnight almost, but do not design to stay much longer. Mr Provost, who came up with me, stayed only a week, namely, till such time as the Hearing before King & Council was over, & left me to manage it since; And I have done what I could in it, but have not quite settled it, The Case standing thus. After the business was fully debated before the King & Council by Counsel on both sides, It was referred (by consent of both parties) to a Trial att Law, & recom~ended to the Lt chief Justice North to setle an issue in a feigned action whereby the matter in controversy may be speedily tried, & wherein the New Charter of Andover is not to be given in evidence att ye Trial, but they are to try the validity of their old charter, & to see if it will enable them att length to remove a Fair from such ground as it has been kept upon not only since the Grant of it: (which is 80 years) but also long before the sd charter. The issue is not settled as yet by my Lt chief Justice (& consequently it is not known where the Trial will be, sc: whether att ye Com~on pleas, or att ye next Assizes att Winchester, which is more p~bable) but is like to be this next week, I have entrusted a Friend to look after it & to give me an account. The Bp of Lincoln & Sr Joseph Williamson are both in good health, I see them this morning: I met with Sr Christofer Philipson accidentally in Westminster Hall two days ago, but doubt, I shall not see him again before I leave the city. I am Sr Your most humble Served Tho: Dixon. These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight: att Rydall-Hall in Westmoreland To be sent by post to Kendall.

Oxon~ Decber: ye 3 (82) Honoured Sr. Missing of Burnyatts (by whom I recd 7l~ for your Son) I wrote to you from London, while I was transacting my business there touching Wayhill Fair, & gave you a short account how the Case stood & what success wee had had before ye King & Council. Since my return to Oxon~ I recd one from you by ye post, for which & your good advice therein, I am very much obliged unto you. I have not resolved as yet what measures to take about Wayhill, but think of judging according to ye assurance I am like to have of ye profits of ye Fair continueing upon ye Glebe (which in all p~bability I shall certainly know either the next Assizes att Winchester, or ye next Term) and the encouragemt & assistance the College will afford me in manageing the Concern & defraying the expense thereof. It has cost me 30l~ & upwards already, but the Provost has p~miss'd that (when I know the whole expense) the College shall assist me, & consider me either by continueing my Grace, or allowance of wood or some other equivalent. So that I know not what more to expect for ye prsent, But shall p~ceed to acquaint you with some more welcome News, namely, with your Sons being elected Tabiter, which favour was conferred upon him on ye first of this Month, to the great joy of all his & your well-wishers, & to the great satisfaction (I prsume) of the electors, they being all unanimous in their Votes for him. He is to be admitted (and will I hope have his Degree too) before ye ending of ye Term on ye 18 of this month: There were 2 more Tabitrs (besides a ffellow & a chaplain) elected with him, sc: one Highmore (who is his Senr) & one Cannon (the provosts Servitor) who is his Junr, as also Simsons & Harrison Junr, whereat I doubt Mr Simson of Kendall will be troubld, especially upon his Sons account: yet as far as I can perceive neither his Son nor Harrison is to be blamed, there being nothing objected either aged their Learning or Morals. So that wee must resolve their missing into something else than their own demerits, I will not undertake to assign ye cause or to meddle with State affairs or ye Intrigues of a Conclave: I am satisfied with your Sons good fortune, & wish him the like the next time he appears as a Candidate for higher promotion in Queens: for he must think of that now & endeavour to qualify himself for it. After his admission into his Tabiters place & expenses of that & his Degree, I shall send you his Accounts, whereby (as also by those you have had already) you'll see, or at least guess, what it has cost you to make him Tabiter & what may serve upon ye like occasion another time. Pray prsent my service to Mr William, & believe me to be Sr Your most obliged Servant Tho: Dixon. These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight att Rydall-Hall near Kendall in Westmoreland prsent. To be sent by post to Lancastr & Kendall

Oxon~ Jan: ye 14th (82/83) Honoured Sr. Yors dated Dec: 15th I received, together with ye enclosed, which I delivered to Mr Provost att his return to ye College two days ago. I was also out of Town (sc: att Weyhill) till ye 5th instant, which occasioned my silence thus long. And now I hope it is not too late, either to wish you an happy New-Year, or to acquaint you that your son is Batchlour of Arts, as well as Tabiter, or to send you his Accounts after such long delays. I have wrote them on the other side & stated them as clearly & punctually as I could, and if there be any mistakes in them they shall be rectified upon the least notice, & the particular Bills shall be likewise sent if you have a mind to them. But I hope you'll find nothing in them but what is moderate, & that your son has not been extravagant. Mr Simsons son & Harrison took their Degrees at ye same time with him, & so put themselves of ye foundation, but (before they did so) endeavours were used in ye behalf of Simson to prvail upon Mr Provost to hearken to an election for him the next Term & to grant him (if he was elected) seniority of Cannon, (according to his standing) But he did not seem inclinable either to the one or the other. So the poor boys must be content & dos as well as they can. I have advised Mr Simson (because I had a letter from him about his Son, which came too late) to continue his Son in ye College till he is Master of Arts, & to lay out for prfermt for him in the mean time, & (if he think fit) to get the next prsentac~on of a good Living for him (if he can) after some ancient Incumbent. And as for Harrison, the new Arch Deacon of Carlisle designs to be as instrumental as he can in p~cureing ye Schoolmasters place of Carlisle for him. As for my own concerns att Wayhill, when I was there lately, the Issue upon which our Trial is to be, (signed by my Lt chief Justice North on ye 11th of 10ber) was sent down from London & also a Copy thereof, with directions how to serve the Bailiff of Andover therewith: which were accordingly put in practise on New Years day, wherewith the Bailiff was not well pleased, but prtended their Counsel was not prsent when it was signed & that it was not according to ye Order of King & Council & that therefore they would prferr a new petition to his Maty: So wee expect to hear how theyl proceed. It seems the Issue (which is to this effect, sc: ) is not according to their mind, though it seems according to ye Order of King & Council, & my Lt Chief Justice that was, apprehended it to be so: and I hope it will prove so notwithstanding their cavils. They fancy it will not do their work, (seeing they have no land upon Weyhill strictly so called, nor ever had any, & wee can make it appear that there was a Fair there long before their Charter, possibly longer than it is since) & do therefore seek for evasions, & are projecting to get a Trial att Barr & a Middlesex Jury, (distrusting their Neighbours) So wee must watch their motions, & look to our wits & be ready for them aged the begin~ing of ye Term. In ye interim, with my respects prsented to Mr William & Mr Fletcher (wn you see him) I remain Sr Your much obliged Friend & humble Servant Tho: Dixon. My duty to my Fathr. I recd his late lettr & shall write ever long. Flamings Accounts betwixt Nov: ye 24 (80) & St Tho: day (82)

column46: Oxon~ Feb. 4. 82/3 Sr I hope you have received ye letter I sent by the post at Xtimas. I took my degree the last term (which was very chargeable to me) and how much I am behind with Mr Dixon I doe not know, but he was telling me that he would give you an account of all, which perhaps you have received already. I am now begun with rendering Aristotle and divinity, and being at a want for good divinity books, I would desire you to send me some in English or rather in Latin if you have any which you can well spair. I also desire you to send me some cloth for a suite with Rich. Burnyeats for I must now (being a rank higher then I was, and keeping better company) go handsomer, and spend more out of pocket, be as careful, and as thrifty as I can: But what I spend more in such things will be spaired in battles, Tutorage, and chamber which will now cost me little or nothing. So having no news worth writing, with my duty to your self, and my love to all my brothers and sisters, I ever remain Your very dutiful son Henry Fleming. I send enclosed an account of my disburstments. For The Right worshipful Sr Daniel Fleming Knight at Rydal-hall near Kendal.

Oxon~ March ye 11th (82/83) Honoured Sr, Since my last I have recd two from you, one by Rich: Dixon on Feb: 27th: & another this morning by ye young Carrier, & having so convenient an opportunity att prsent as the coming down of Mr Mayor of Kendall, I could not omit sending this short answer to them both. Before I left London I found myself obliged to retract what I had wrote to my ffather concerning my coming into ye Country this Spring, I perceived my business would not give way to such a journey & must therefore defer it to a better convenience. I hope to see a good issue of my affair by ye middle of July, if it be looked after & well managed in ye mean time. I think I told you in my last that wee had a hearing before my Lt Keeper on ye 17th of ffebr: & that some amendmts were made in ye Issue which he had signed by ye consent of both pties, & that they had accepted of ye s~d Issue, so that nothing was wanting now to bring it to a Trial, but an agreemt on both sides as to place & time of Trial, whereat it yet sticks. They are for ye Barr & a Middlesex Jury, but wee are for a Hantshire Jury wherever it is tried. I am glad it was not tried ye last Assizes, because Mr Provost met with & showed me a paper lately (amongst Dr Pottrs paprs) touching ye valuac~on of some Livings in Hantshire (given by the late King) & amongst ye rest of Way (now Wayhill) in the pticulars of whose firstfruits & Tenths (as they were rated 26 Hen: 8vi:) the standing of ye Fair is therein reasoned att 40s. which thing if it can be made out by ye original Record or Book of Taxation (as ye Provost dos not doubt but it may) it will do us signal service, & possibly make out a better Title for ye College than either the Hospital of Ewelme or the Corporac~on of Andover can prtend to: but they must know nothing of this 'till it come to the push. Mr Provost has given ye Company time to consider what theyl do about ye charges. They have anothr thing in hand att prsent sc: Mr Nicholsons concern, Sr Joseph having made it his request to ye College that he may return to his ffellowship, & hold His ArchDeaconry & prebendary with it, att which they are a little startled (as also att some other pticulars in Sr Josephs lettr touching ye College, which they fancy Mr Nicholson informed him in) & have sent up Mr Crostwhait as an envoy to Sr Joseph, the result of whose message wee shall know ever long. In ye mean time he may suffer bye being absent in ye North. I shall go to Weyhill before Easter. My service to Mr William & Mr Fletcher when you see him. I am Sr Your much obliged Friend & humble Served Tho: Dixon. These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight att Rydall-hall near Kendall. in Westmoreland. prsent.

column46: Oxon~ March 12. 82/3 Sr Yours of Feb. 15. I have received, and that of March ye 1st came to my hand yesterday, and according to your order I consulted with my Mercer and Taylor about a suit, and I find by there great bills that I cannot have a good cloth suit here as cheap as my last was, though I see by Mr Simpson's note, with carraige and making it amounts to 3l~. So that I think it best way to have it ready made from London if you can conveniently, which will certainly be of ye newest fashion, and I believe as cheap. As concerning ye colour of coat and waist-coat I am very indifferent, if not black, or very light which will be too flaunting. Mr Simpson of Kendal went this morning towards Cambridge to get a new Vicar for Kendal, receiving a letter last night concerning Mr Stanfords death. Mr Dixon is yett in ye College, nor doe I hear any thing of his going into ye country. So with my duty to your self, and my love to all my brothers and sisters, I ever remain Your very dutiful son Henry Fleming. A measure of my coat; one yard wide in ye breast; one yard wide bate nail in ye waist; one yard and almost quarter long; half ell and nail long in ye sleeve; and a neck to ye coat. The breeches half yard and half quarter long. For The Right worshipful Sr Daniel Fleming Knight at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

Oxon~ March ye 24 (82/3) Honoured Sr. Having wrote to you by Mr Mayor of Kendall on the 11th instant in answer to your 2 last, I have not much to add by ye Bearer, only our hearty Thanks for your Token, & that out of your 7l~ I received by ye Bearer, I paid the Mercer on the 20th instant 5l~ - 15s. which cleared all his dues till that time, & I have 20s still in my hands to be answered to your Son as he shall have occasion. I told you in my last, that I could not possibly visit the North so soon as I once projected, I must see the business of Wayhill in a better posture before I leave it to itself. I hinted something to you in my last touching a papr Mr Provost had met with, the original Record whereof I have sent to enquire after in ye Remembrancers Office, & if it can be met with (as Mr Provost dos not doubt but it may) wee shall be subtle enough for the Body politic. When I have had an account from London I design to go into Hantshire to hasten the Trial, & if wee find the Record I shall not fear to try it where they please, if they will not be brought to our terms. It seems Mr Nicholson was this day denied the liberty of returning to his ffellowship notwithstanding Sr Josephs intercession, but it is said he recd such satisfaction from ye Messenger who went up, that he referred the business wholly to ye Society, So his year of Grace ends tomorrow. They have not discussed my business as yet. Capt Tempest of Durham has been in town a pretty while. He came up about a Nephew of his (one Shutleworth of Yorkshire) whom he entered fellow Com~oner of Trinity College about half a year ago, His mother came up also with him & has continued in town with him, but that did not hinder his falling in love with ye president of Magdalens only daughter, to whom he was married 10 weeks ago & upwards, and now they are to go down to Faucett in Yorkshire with ye Capt & his Mother (the Capts Sister) if she be able to travel this next week: The young Lady is said to be with child, though she is not 16, and he is not above 17 years of age. John Tredeskins Rarities are come down from London by water. The Elaboratory (which Some call the Knick-knackatory) is almost finished & ready to receive them. Dr Plot who is to be Supervisor of ye Elaboratory brought them down. My service to Mr William I am Sr Your much obliged Friend & Served Tho: Dixon. Mr Ward is come down to take possession of Skeleton in Cumberland which he has in lieu of Hampton Poyle. These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight att Rydall-hall near Kendall: in Westmoreland. prsent.

column46: Oxford. March. 26th 83 Worthy Sr Since you are pleased to confer that honour upon me, as to make me one of those many that stand obliged to your goodness, I could not without a proof of my own ingratitude omit this opportunity of thankfully acknowledging the many fresh tokens of your love. I doe ingenuously confess, that when I set pen to paper, my mind told me how mean a requital a few bare words are, and the danger of incurring your displeasure by this my boldness: but when on the other side I considered that thanks are the only requital I can make; and that it was better to stand accused of presumption, then undergo the censure of ingratitude; then I resolved to give you this trouble; which (except your goodness interpose) is unpardonable. Be pleased therefore to accept, what I can only give, my humblest thanks; and believe me to be, with I really am Noble Sr Ire most obliged Servant and Obedient Godson Hen: Brougham ffor The right Worshipful Sr Daniel Fleming att Rydal nigh Kendall in Westmrland These

Oxon~ July ye 12th (83) Honoured Sr. I have been so much employed of late about my Law concerns, that I hope you'll pardon my neglect of writing. I returned from London on ye 7th instant only, since which time I recd yors dated June ye 22d, as also 5s for a Token, for which I must thank you in the name of some others as well as myself: & ought to have done so the last return of the Carrier Burnyatts for the Token you sent then, but it seems the multiplicity of business I had upon me, made me forget it, as well as myself. I am att prsent also involved in troubles which will obleige me to be shorter than I designed. When I was att London I brought our business to a Trial att Winchester Assizes on ye 17th instant, & it so falls out that the Bp of Winton has his Triennial Visitac~on att Andover that same day, & he has warned me to preach ye Sermon, So I have both my hands full att prsent, being to examine Witnesses & to p~vide a Sermon aged the time. I set forward this morning towards Wayhill, so that I have only time to subscribe my self Sr Your much obliged Friend & Served Tho: Dixon. These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight att Rydall-hall in Westmoreland. prsent.

column46: Oxford July 14th 83 Worthy Sr If the sense of my duty could not excite in me the least thought of kissing your hand with a letter; yet were I in gratitude bound not to omit any opportunity of writing, that I might make some (though never sufficient) acknowledgments of those many favours you are pleased to bestow on me. There be some so solicitous how to quit themselves of their obligac~ons; but yet so discourteously ungrateful, that scorning to be obliged to any, can willingly embrace a favour, but yet hate the person that confers it. Be assured, Sir, that I am none of that number; for the sense of your goodness and mine own unworthiness doe exceed the height of expression; and I have always accounted it a great honour to stand obliged to that generosity, which has imposed the same fate upon many others as upon my self. Accept my humble duty to ire self, & pray give my service to all my . I am Worthy Sr Ire most dutiful Godson & humble Servant Hen: Brougham. For The Right Worshipful Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydall nigh Kendal in Westmrland

And concerning the 5s which you mention in your letter that you doe not know what became of, Mr Dixon received which was to be spent also among ye fellows, but he neglected to acquaint you with it. So having no news here worth writing, with my duty to your self and my love to all my brothers and sisters, I ever remain Your very dutiful Son Henry Fleming. column46: Oxon~ July 18-1683. Sr Although I writ to you lately by Burnyeat (which I hope is come safe to your hand) I could not pass by so fair an opportunity, in not troubleing this bearer with a line to you (being one Mr Teasdel our Senior Tabiter) who promised to see you, whom I desire you would make welcome. I have had some thoughts this long time to desire you (but never durst be so bold till now) to let me come down this winter to see you, which would be a great ease to me, seeing in that time we undergo so much hardship here; and also little loss that season of the year, by reason of its coldness being so unfitt for study, and very chargeable. So hoping that you will consider of it, with my duty to yourself, and my love to all my brothers and sisters, I ever remain Your very dutiful Son Henry Fleming For The right worshipful Sr Daniel Fleming Knight at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.
