column46: Oxon~ Aug. 13. 1683. Sr I could not deny Mr Dixon aboue all others a letter to you, although I writ very lately by Mr Teasdell a Tabiter of our College, which I hope is come safe to your hands: in which I desired you to let me come into the country about Michaelmas to stay this next winter with you. Nor doe I much question but Mr Dixon can satisfy you what a great help it will be to me to pass over a winter, without the hardships which we always undergo here at that time of the year. We have no news here but Mr Dixon or Mr Rooke can acquaint you with better than I, so that I will not now presume to trouble you with any. So with my duty to your self, and my love to all my brothers and sisters, I ever remain Sr Your very dutiful Son Henry Fleming. For The right worshipful Sr Daniel Fleming Knight att Rydal-Hall near Kendal These.

Oxon~ Oct: ye 21st (83) or rather London. Oct. 23 (83). Honoured Sr. I received yours by your Son about 2 days ago, wherein though you were pleased to own our visiting of you as an obligac~on, yet certainly the engagement lay on our part, & the kindnesses received ought to have been acknowledged by us long here this, especially by me; But, I hope, you'll pardon the neglect, seeing I have been employed in receiving of money, & in hastening to manage & look after the p~fitts of my Fair. Wee spun out our journey so long (by taking York & Northampton in our road) that I stayed but one night in Oxon~, after which short stay Mr Langton was so kind as to go along with me to Wayhill, where he saw sheep enough, though he had mutton little enough at ye parsonage house. I could have afforded him more, if the 30000 sheep which stood on ye Glebe Land had been all my own: But the sight of them did well enough seeing their standing brought in 65l~i to the Rector. The Bailiff of Andover was not well pleased with the sight. It seems he & his brethren will attic us once more, So I doubt I must make the other journey to London very speedily. I recd 5s of your Son which shall be spent upon ye company either before I go or when I return. Your Son is nothing in my debt. There was something due to him att the last accounts sent to you, which he has had out since in Study Rent over me. Isle advise & befriend him all I may, being obliged thereunto upon several accounts. I have no news to send you but that the humour of Translating Books into English goes on very much in Oxon~, Cornelius Nepos is a coming out done by several hands, & Erasmus's Mori Encomium is out already. Some say that Moses Pit has in 3 several Editions of ye Com~on prayer Book lately printed at Oxon~ omitted the Injunction touching the Surplice, for which he is much blamed. Some say that he is lately engaged in a project about the Cole Mines in Cornwall, which may retard the progress of ye Atlas. My service to Mr William &c. I am Sr. Your much obliged Friend & humble Served Tho: Dixon Mr Langton prsents his humble service to you. These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight: att Rydall-hall near Kendall. in Westmoreland. prsent.

column46: Honoured Godfather I should be a rebel to gratitude, if I were not proud of this opportunity. That your good son is pleased to take the trouble upon him of presenting this to your hand, is a greater kindness than I can any way deserve; yet it is the least of those many favours I have received att his hands. Modesty forbids me presume to write so often; but the deep sense of my debt to you stifles it's dictates, and bids me purchase gratitude though with the censure of presumption. I shall not trouble you with repeated acknowledgmts of your goodness to me; since it is so great as exceeds all expression; and in such a case silence is the best eloquence. Only pray satisfy my ambition so far as to honour me with the titles of Worthy Sr Your most obedient Godson and humble Servant Hen: Browham. Oxford. Octobr 26th 83. For The Right Worshipful Sr Daniel Fleming att Rydal nigh Kendall in Westmrland These

London Feb: ye 19 (83/4) Honoured Sr. I know not what apology to make for my long silence, the late cold weather is too stall a Theme: yet I can lay the blame no where else, except my absence from Oxon~ & great distance in the Country from a Post Town. I confess I made a shift to write 2 or 3 lines to my Father in the sharp season, but it was upon business, and for a horse, which I desired him to send me up att your Sons return, & to let him have the convenience of riding of him up: And I hope heel procure a good one, as well for my sake as ire Sons. I believe your Son need not hasten his return till the weather be milder & the ways better. I fancy he could not have been with you in a more seasonable winter, I mean, as to the prjudice & hinderance of his Studdys. His fellow Tabiters have not made much of it I fancy, except in the way of expense & charge for fire & Shoo leather. ffive of the Seniors determine this Lent, & there are 4 more of our house: besides others that are expected. The small pox abate very much in Oxon~. I returned thither out of Hantshire & Glocestershire about a week ago. I found little alterac~on in ye College, only Louder the poor child was dead, & Mr Provost had been indisposed for some time & Mr Crostwhait had had a spice of ye Gout. It seems the Vice-Chancellour has p~hibited the Booksellrs from selling Cornelius Nepos (lately translated by several hands) by reason of some expressions in ye preface; He has also found fault with another preface before the first part of Plutarchs Morals translated by several hands. Some ffellows of Colleges who were wittier than they should have been att an unseasonable time of the night & are said to have drolled the She-Innkeeper of the Mitre (who was a papist) to death, were sconced 40s for Noctivagation & forced to recant or ask forgiveness in congregac~on. Dr Crowther the principal of St Mary Hall was arrested in his Lodgings upon a Wrote of Rebellion out of Chancery for contempt of ye Court, in refusing to appear, & to stand to the award of some Arbitrators, which he consented to nominate, touching the setting of a Fine, which he & Tenant of the Corps for his prebend, could not agree upon. It is said the principal of Edmund Hall, having got the prsentac~on of a good Living, will resign the Hall. I hear since I came to this Town that Dr Mill & Mr Tompson of Bristol are candidates for the Deanery of Bristol (worth about 120l~ p~ an~u~) now vacant. I was sum~on'd up to a Hearing which wee are to have in chancery on the 21st instant, The result whereof I shall give my father an account of, & shall defer writing to him till then. In ye mean time pray Give my duty to him, as also my respects to your Sons. I am Sr Your much obliged Friend & Served Tho: Dixon. These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming knight: att Rydall-Hall in Westmoreland. prsent.

Oxon~ Apr. ye 28 (84). Honoured Sr I happened to go for Hantshire before your last (dated March ye 8 & sent by ye Northampton Carrier) came to your Sons hands, so it continued with your Son till my return from London on ye 25th instant. I designed to return from Wayhill prsently after Easter, but I was detained upon the account of a Com~ission for examinac~on of ancient Witnesses in our cause, which was executed ye week after Easter & held for 3 or 4 days, and then the Term drawing on some occasions fell out which drew me towards London, namely, the design of our Advrsaries to set aside some part of my Lt Keepers last order on Feb. ye 21st, sc: that part of it which related to a Hantshire Jury: And they did accordingly attempt it att ye begin~ing of ye Term, but could not prvail. So wee have forced them to concur in striking a Hampshire Jury of Gentlemen, and the Trial is to be att ye Exchequer Barr the first Wednesday in ye next Term or on June ye 4th. I have had some terms of accom~odation offered to me & the College by some of ye Corporac~on, & they would willingly (I believe) secure half (if not more) to me or ye College, if I would desist, & leave them to contend with ye Hospital as to their right, but this is a point that must be well weighed and advised upon. I have acquainted ye Provost (betwixt whom & a great part of ye ffellows there's no good undrstanding att prsent) with ye whole p~ceedings & how the case stands. I must go over to Wayhill again some time this week So I have no time to manage (or so much as think on) any such designs or intrigues as you fancied by your last I might be engaged in. I have not seen Mr Langton since I was at cold Ashton (where wee lived with a Tenant) nor heard from him but once. He is att Bristol att prsent with his Relac~ons. Wee spent your 5s Token before I went last to Wayhill, & I was desired to return you thanks for it long here this. On Thursday last the Vicechancellour admitted Mr Crostwhait into ye principality of Edmund Hall, he is also Provostplace in ye College again, & not Mr Lancaster. Mr Thomson is Dean of Bristol after all, but there wants a new Bp still. I need not tell you by whom the late Northern Prefermts are supplied, or that I am Sr Your obliged Friend & Served Tho: Dixon. My service (I pray) to Mr William, Mr Daniel, Mr Fletcher &c. These in all 5d To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight att Rydall-hall near Kendall. in Westmoreland. prsent.

column46: Oxon. June 14. 1684. Sr Yours of May 14 I received of my Cousin Goo. Fletcher and was very glad to hear that all was well with you. Mr Dixon has not been in Oxon~ since yours came to my hand; but we hear that he has got ye trial, at which how things were carried, we have such an imperfect account, yt I shall not trouble you with it. Mr Todd intends for ye country very shortly to be ye Bish~ of Carlile's chaplin. Mr Will~ Graham was the last week here, but he staid only three days, and so returned to London. The differences which lately happened in or College are (I hope) composed: For Mr Crosthwaite is both Principle of St Edmond Hall, and fellow of or College, which was for a long time denied him by Mr Provost and some of the fellows. I have sent you a note of my disburstments, that you may know the better what to send, though I have not payed all off, which I should doe very shortly, if I could, ye year ending the next week. I am behind with my Mercer for somethings which I had before I took my journey, and somethings since, almost 3l~: and I doe also want now a Batchlours gown which will cost 4l~ more at ye least: And the next term I must begin to doe my exercise towards my degree, which will be partly chargeable. So that I hope you will be pleased to supply me accordinly by Burnyeat, with whom I shall return a bill of particulars. So this with my duty to your self and my love to all my brothers and sisters is all, from Sr Your very dutiful Son Henry Fleming. For Sr Daniel Fleming att Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

column37: rector of Grasmere 1685, rector of Asby 1694-1728
column39: The Flemings in Oxford Being Documents Selected from the Rydal Papers in Illustration of the Lives and Ways of Oxford Men 1650-1700. Vol. II 1680-1690. Ed. by Magrath, John Richard. Oxford Historical Society 62. 1913.
column46: Oxon~. June 28th - 1684. Sr Having so fit an opportunity I could not pass it by without writing, though I writ lately by the post, which I hope you received before Burnyeat left the country. I have little more to acquaint you withal, but that the last week at a general meeting of the trainbands in this county, on night two scholars (viz. one Willis of Christ Church Coll. Batch~. of Arts, and one Bolds of Martin Coll~. com~oner) being a little in their drink, affronting the guards, and the Earl of Abbington the Lord Leutennant of this country, was sent to the castle that night by the Proctor, and publicly expelled the University, by the Vice-Chancellor the next day. Dr Mill of or Coll~. is lately married, and has got near 3000l~ fortune. This with my duty to your self, and love to all my brothers and sisters, is all from Your very dutiful Son Henry Fleming. The bearer is Mr Dixon's brother. For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

Oxon~ July ye 14 (84) Honoured Sr Though the Bearer leaves us in a very busy time, yet I can~ot omit returning you thanks for your continued kindness & bounty in sending us your old Token, wherewith wee have not rememberd you as yet (by reason of my absence att Weyhill till the begin~ing of ye Act & now it is scarce over) but shall do very shortly. I have little News to send you but that Mr Provost went into Wales on friday last, & that the Vicechancellour being sick, Dr Berry (Rector of Exeter College) supplied his place this Act. He has threatend to expel the 2 Terraefilij, the latter whereof retorted upon him in ye same words when he said to him "Impono tibi silentiu~" . They both of them p~ceeded contrary to ye Vicechancellours Deputy's order, so I know not what will become of them, though the former (sc: Mr Bell of Magdalens, the other being of Lincoln) was ingenious & very mimicall. They both of them had a fling att our new Principal, & the latter was severe upon him. The one of them made smart remarks upon Dr Plot & the Associates Curiosoru~ lately erected in Oxon~ but especially upon ye Dr for his covetousness & dodgeing with ye world as to his History of Staffordshire. One was brought in deposeing that he met Dr Plot carrying his Knickknackatory (a Nickname for ye Elaboratory) for a Rare Show to Bristol Fair. I leave the rest to Mr Tod of Univrsity the new Bps chaplain, whom you'll see att ye Assizes. As to my own concern I prsume my Father has acquainted you that nothwithstanding or 2 Verdicts wee are yet to have a Hearing before my Lt Keeper the next Term, which Hearing will, as I hope, end in a Decree. Till it be over I shall defer building & other unnecessary projects. My respects to Mr William & all with you. I am Sr Your much obliged Served Tho: Dixon. These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight att Rydall-Hall near Kendal. in Westmoreland. prsent.

column37: clergy lower: prebendary of Asgarby; professional: fellow of Queen's College, Oxford
column39: The Flemings in Oxford Being Documents Selected from the Rydal Papers in Illustration of the Lives and Ways of Oxford Men 1650-1700. Vol. II 1680-1690. Ed. by Magrath, John Richard. Oxford Historical Society 62. 1913.
column46: Oxon~ October. 1st 84. Honoured Godfather When I reflect upon the inestimable kindness you did me in procuring my admission into the Church, and on the continued course of ire goodness to me; I am ready to sink under the deep sense of my unworthiness, as being now no more able to return ire favours, than I was then, when least able. But second thoughts tell me, ire goodness is not mercenary, and that it is most apparent there, where there's the least prospect of retaliation. Upon these grounds I build all my satisfaction; and shall content my self with barely acknowledging my debt, till other circumstances have put me in a way of making some discharge. I presume this Gentleman the Bearer is not so much a stranger to you, but that you have heard of his great merits, and good behaviour in ye Coll: and with all how badly they have been rewarded. The thoughts of this would disencourage me in my studies; but that I hope though I am less deserving, yet I may have more friends than he had. One of whom I hope Mr Provost will be; to whom a word from you in my behalf would do much. Pray pardon this presumption, and accept the duty of Ire most obedient Godson & Humble Servant Hen: Browham. To The Right Worshipful Sr Daniel Fleming att Rydal-hall near Kendal in Westmrland.

Oxon~ Oct: ye 16 (84). Honoured Sr I received yors by Burnyatts, and 5s by your Son, for the former I am solely obliged to you: but the Society share with me in the obligac~on for the latter: And wee all wish for an opportunity of being able to make some requiteall for all your Tokens & kindnesses. I dare say your Son need not have doubted of future Promotion in ye House as soon as he had been capable: But seeing he is in a fair way of having it elsewhere, wee must submit to your disposeall of him, and I wish him as good prferment (in due time) as the North can afford, & there is as good there as elsewhere, if a man can catch it, as I hope he will. You do well of thinking to continue him att ye Univrsity 3 or 4 years longer: It will qualify him for what you bestow upon him & what he may have, and I shall not be wanting to assist him, what I may, while I am in the College, & afterwards as often as heel do me the kindness to visit me. I must be for London again this Term, wee are to have a Hearing before my Lt Keeper on ye 7th of next Month, if no new motions on ye 1st Day of ye Term defer it, I have not been served with a Quo Warranto, though Mr Drake has, So wee know not what they drive att in divideing of us, but wee suspect the worst: yet I hope wee shall be able to deal with them either jointly or separately. I have little news to send you but that the Bp of Oxon~ returned lately from visiting the Bp of Winton, who has been much indisposed of late, but is, as he said, on ye mending hand, and that there are some Candidates for the Principality of Edmund Hall, because it is supposed, that the Provost will declare it vacant shortly, the 6 months being expired which the Hall Statutes allow of for its consistency with a Fellowship. My humble service to Sr George & Mr Fletcher wn you see them, as also to Mr William & all with you. I am Sr Your much obliged Friend & Servant Tho: Dixon. These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight att Rydall-hall near Kendall in Westmoreland prsent

column37: rector of Grasmere 1685, rector of Asby 1694-1728
column39: The Flemings in Oxford Being Documents Selected from the Rydal Papers in Illustration of the Lives and Ways of Oxford Men 1650-1700. Vol. II 1680-1690. Ed. by Magrath, John Richard. Oxford Historical Society 62. 1913.
column46: Queens Oxon Fibre. 28. 1684/5 Sr On Monday night last I got into Oxon~ very well, and on Wednesday I received my box with the money: but I have heard nothing yet from Rob. Harrison of Grasmere concerning my horse, so that (I fear) I shall be forced to keep the horse here till Burnyeat return. We have had an election here lately both for Fellows and Tabiters: at which Mr Teasdal and Mr Allan Fisher was elected Fellows, and my cos. Browham and three more elected Tabiters. The commissioners appointed to examine the difference in our Coll. sat last week several days, but has not made any end. This with my duty to your self and my love to all my Brothers and Sisters. I am Your very obedient Son Henry Fleming. For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal-Hall near Kendal These

Oxon~. March ye 22 (84) Honoured Sr. Yors dated ye 15th of ye last I recd only 2 or 3 days ago, by reason I went to Wayhill a little before your Son arrived at Oxon & did not return till very lately. So I have not much news to send you. I was att ye election for Kts of ye Shire for Hantshire on ye 16 instant, wee chose my Lt Cambden (son to ye E. of Gainsborough) & my Lt Wiltshire (second son to ye Marquess of Winchestr) And the city of Winton chose Roger LeStrange & one Hunsy for their Burgesses the same day. I hope my Law concern is now almost att an end, his Maty having been graciously pleased to cause the Quo Warranto to be with drawn upon a Hearing (which was the first of that kind) before him att Council Board on ye 11 of last month & to order that his Name should not be made use of in behalf of ye Town, but that the matter should be left to ye Law. So they moved My Lt Keeper since to grant them a new Trial att ye Com~on Pleas Barr by a foreign Jury, & not by a Hantshire Jury att ye Kings Bench as in a formr ordr of chancery: But upon p~useing some Records, which his Ldship had not seen before, he refused to grant them any Trial att all, but ordered a Hearing only before him as soon as ye course of ye Court will p~mitt. Upon which Hearing (eithr ye next Term or ye Term following) wee hope to obtain a Decree, And then all affrightmts & discouragemts from looking after other momentous concerns may possibly be over. If my fathr had had Quo Warrantos & such like Law Monstrs to grapple with, I fancy they would have retarded him in his late adventures. But I must think of getting a better house before I get a Housekeeper, I have been discoursing with Workmen & have ordered Materials to be laid in, & shall go on this Sum~er as I can spare money. I may possibly have some othr occasion for money att ye Act. So if wee can get some costs after all, theyl do us a kindness. It passed currant in Hantshire lately that ye Bailiff of Andover was arrested att London, after he & othrs had prsented ye Address, for costs upon our account, but it was upon some other. The stage fell down at Andover when they p~claim'd ye King which has been looked upon since as an ill omen to them. Pray give my service to Mr William, & to Sr George & your nephew Mr Henry Fletcher wn you see them. I am Sr Your Friend & Served in his power Tho: Dixon. These To the Right Worpfull Sr Daniel Fleming Knight at Rydall Hall near Kendall in Westmoreland prsent

column46: Oxon~. Sept. 12 85 Sr About five weeks since I received a letter from you, which I answered shortly after: but I have heard nothing out of the country since then. Burnyeat being to come up shortly, I would desire you to send some money by him; for I must have a gown, cassock and sash, and also pay two quarters battles, and several other things before winter be done, which will far exceed that money which I have in my hand; therefore if you would be pleased to send £20 by him (which you were saying you would allow me yearly, besides what I have fro~ Gresmere) I will manage it so, as to be very little troublesome to you. Sir Goo. Fletcher has sent for my Cos. George into the country, who begins his journey next friday, but the reason why he sends for him so suddenly, we cannot judge. Sr Lionel Jenkins's body is brought hither on Teusday next, where he is to lay in state 2 or 3 days, and then be buried in Jesus Coll. Chapel, to which College he has left 500l p~ ann~. Sir John Lowthers brother of Louder was ent'red in or College the last week. Mr Provost is to be elected Vice Chancellor again the next week. We have no news here but the death of ye Lt Keeper, and that Sr John Churchill the Moister of the Rolls is laying a dyeing. Here is lately come forth the Life of Christ written by Mr Walker, head of University Coll. in 4to price 5s. This with my duty to your self and love to all my Brothers and sisters, I am Ire very dutiful son Hen. Fleming. For Sr Daniel Fleming a Member of Parliament at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

column37: rector of Grasmere 1685, rector of Asby 1694-1728
column39: The Flemings in Oxford Being Documents Selected from the Rydal Papers in Illustration of the Lives and Ways of Oxford Men 1650-1700. Vol. II 1680-1690. Ed. by Magrath, John Richard. Oxford Historical Society 62. 1913.
column46: Queens Coll~. Oxon~. November. 21th 85. Sr Yours of the 17th instant and also that by Burnyeat I have received with 10l, which I am afraid will fall a little short of my necessities; yet I shall endeavour to make it go as far as possible: our want of an Act this year, did us not (as you suppose) any great kindness; for what an Act would have cost in treats and such like idle expenses, we were forced to pay in money to the University treasury, and College library. The life of Christ sold very well here a while at first, but being afterwards something better examined, has since been prohibited by the Vice Chancellor, for leaning too much towards Popery in several places of it. So that I sent you none down by Burnyeat. I would have writ to you ere this, but that I was not certain of your being in London till I received your last. This with my duty to yourself I am Your most dutiful Son Hen. Fleming. Since the writing hereof we had the news here of the Parliament being prorogued, and not knowing where you lodged I thought this ye surest way to direct it. For Sr Daniel Fleming a member of Parliament To be left with Mr John Nicholson At Mr Sills house in the Cloisters At Westminster. London.

column46: Rose, Dec. 19, 1685. Sr I have recd yours by this bearer, together with Sr Jo: Vaughans Reports for which I return you many thanks, and will be very careful, not only to keep it clean, but to return it also in due time. As for ye Bearer, I will upon your recommendation try what may be done for him, though I think he has not deserved it either from you or me. I shall wish you a good journey, and good success at Conishead, but I can hardly think you will have the company of ye Oxford scholar thither, for he continues still very ill: I had a letter on Tuesday last from Sr George, wherein he tells me he has kept his bed ever since his coming home; eats nothing; and is already grown very weak; and that they had sent for Dr Gilpin to him. On Thursday Mr Todd went over to see him, who tells me he is so very much weakened that he is not able to walk over ye floor without 2 supporting him; that he found there not only Dr Gilpin, but another young Doctor, one Pearson who lives at Penrith or thereabout. Yesterday my Wife and I went over to Carlisle, to make a visit to Mris Rainbow, which occasioned the bearers stay a day longer: we dined at ye Castle with ye Governor (for so everybody stiles him) who lives and eats splendidly. With mine and my wife's humble service to yourself, and our true respects to all yours now with you, not forgetting the young Parson at Oxford, I remain ever Sr Your most faithful Served Tho. Carliol. For Sr Daniel Fleming these at Rydall.

column39: The Flemings in Oxford Being Documents Selected from the Rydal Papers in Illustration of the Lives and Ways of Oxford Men 1650-1700. Vol. II 1680-1690. Ed. by Magrath, John Richard. Oxford Historical Society 62. 1913.
column46: Rose, Apr. 15, 1686 Worthy Sr I have rec'd yours, with an enclosed from Mr Farrington, for whom I have a good respect, but cannot possibly serve him upon this occasion, being long since engaged by promise to Mr Banks to endeavour his promotion fro~ St Bees to Appleby when yt School should become void, and accordingly I have now lately recom~ended him to ye College (who have ye sole power of Electing) but what they will do in it I cannot tell, having not as yet rec'd any answer from them. You have heard (I perceive) of ye death of our late Deane, and within a very few days after dyed his Father in law Sr Jose: Craddock. Yesterday I rec'd the news of ye Archbp of York's being dead of ye small pox: he administerd ye Com~union on Good Friday, preached on Easter-day, and dyed on ye Sunday after. Who will succeed him is not yet known, but Father Graham has already kissed ye Kings hand for ye Deanery of Carlisle. Mr Philip Musgrave is now lying dangerously ill of ye small pox, but they begin I hear to hope well of him. I am glad to hear you are all well at Rydall, and will be glad to see Mr Fleming here; pray tell him I rec'd his kind Letter, and return him many thanks for it. My wife gives you her service, and I am ever Sr Your most faithful Servant Tho. Carliol. The Earl of Anglesey (that great Statesman) is lately dead. For Sr Daniel Fleming these at Rydall.

Sr I recd yrs, with ire approbation of my setting up a Carrier betwixt Kendal & Wthaven, which is a grt confirmation to me. I doe not expect to p~fect ye design at first, & concur with you it will be better done by others than by ye Kendal Carrier. I hear of one Tyson near you a sufficient Man, but ye place where it will be best done is at Keswick, for there is but 4 days time to go & return, so ye middle way is ye best, & I hear of one Hobson there. I have writ to Dr Grey abt it, & pray doe you advise me. Ire acct of ye Bills of Mortality is very exact for 85, I cld have wished ye several Months had been so many Years backward, for ye total of each year is al I desire, which if cast up in ye Book as I suppose they are, is less labour than ye p~ticular Months of one Year, but I will not give you a further trouble living at a distance, I will get Dr Grey who is upon ye place to doe it for me. I have sent you a Barometer by Greenwood ye Carrier which will be in Kendal on Wednesday next, cost thirty shillings; ye Philosophical Transactions are Six Volumes, 4 in Oldenburgs time which cost me 20s p~ Volume. 2 since, something cheaper, now if you have only 7 of ye whole number I know not whether to advise you to make them up, but if 7 since Oldenburg, it were not amiss if you did. let me know ire com~ands & I shall serve you. Kebles Reports are in English 3 vol. folo. price about 50s but of no grt esteem. I am Sr Ire most affect. Kinsman & served J. Louder Land. Ap. 24, 86. The Provost of Queens has writ me this post, yt they have removed Mr Banks from St Bees to Appleby, had I been acquainted with it, my temper is too well known to hinder ye Advancemt of any related to me; but after with I have done not to be consulted in it, nor how to supply St Bees does a little trouble me, & ye more yt they say tic by my Lt Bpp of Carlisles Advice. For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal Kendal Westmerland

column46: Oxon~ May 16 1686. Sr I have not writ this long time by reason we had no news till now worth troubling you with all. I received 2s 6d from Mr Dover which you sent. The late differences in this Coll. which we all thought had been composed are now near as ill as ever: for Dr Crosthwaite has very lately appealed to the Queen, and on Thursday last Mr Provost and Dr Mill went to London about it, but how ill ye event may be to ye Coll: is yet unknown. We have four University men who declare themselves Papists, and has lately got Protections; a copy of which I have enclosed for you. The other day I was with Dr Hide, who is very much my friend, and I was telling him of my Lt Chancellor's promises, and he told me that he thought they signified very little, unless I could get the promise of some one particular place, as a Prebend of Gloucester which is like to fall very shortly and of some value, or some other place; for he has so many Clergy men always about him, yt some or other is still ready to catch whatever falls. With my duty to your self and love to my brothers and sisters. I am Your most dutiful son Hen. Fleming. For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

column39: The Flemings in Oxford Being Documents Selected from the Rydal Papers in Illustration of the Lives and Ways of Oxford Men 1650-1700. Vol. II 1680-1690. Ed. by Magrath, John Richard. Oxford Historical Society 62. 1913.
column46: Rose June 3, 1686. Worthy Sr, I was much ashamed to return you your printed news from Scotland (brought me by your neighbor Mr Walker) withed so much as thanks for it, or anything of an answer to your kind letter by him, but ye blame of it must lie upon him, not me; for his hast to be at Yanwith yt night (and it was then 6 of ye clock) would not allow me any time at all to write; nor could he be prevailed with to stay all night though I importuned him. I am sorry I could not give him any hopes of Cliburne, ye thing having been long since promised: though, as yet, ye old Gentleman holds out, and possibly may do so (as I hear) for some years more. Your news of your Rival's having recd a dismissio~ was very surprising, and I should be glad to know whether it holds or no, for I have not heard anything at all (either of it or ought else) from Hutton. I do not so much as know whether my Lady Mary be yet returned out of Yorkshire; but I am told, wn she does return, Sr To: Fenwick and his Lady comes with her, and intend to be our neighbours, in the Deanery at Carlisle, rather than return to Bywell. You have heard of Mr Obadiah Walker (Master of University Coll:) his having at last declared himself a Romish Priest; and of his Mates having Dispensed with him and 3 other persons in Oxford to hold their places there, non obstante ye 25 and 30 Car. 2di the 1. 5. 13. 23. 27. 29. 35. Eliz. and ye 1 and 3 Jac. 1mi. He has also dispensed with one Mr Adieu: Slater, Rector of Putney, non obstante ye 13. 14. 17. Car: 2di and ye 21 and 28 Hen: 8vi and ye 1. 5. 13. 14. 23. 27. 29. 35 Eliz: and ye 1. 3. 7. Jacobi. From Oxford, Dr Mill to our Arched. writes thus - Thus far ye Doctor. At Edinburgh there has been hard tugging. In their Answer to ye Kings Letter, wr they say They will go as great Lengths as their Consciences will allow ; I hear it was put to ye vote whether ye word Duty should not be made use of instead of Conscience , but tic said Conscience carried it by great Odds. We were told last week in our London News-letter yt in all probability ye Parlt in Scotland would consent to with ye K. had demanded of them : but on Tuesday last Bas: Fielding sent me word That the Question (after a long debate) having been put on Thursday last, whether ye Laws aged Roman Cath: should be repealed, it was carried in ye Negative by very many votes, (some say above 10 to one.) In Ireland, they say, things go worse and worse: insomuch yt ye Protestants in many parts begin to be fearful and jealous of their safety; and yt ye price of Lands there, from 15 or 16 years purchase, is fallen to 8. Last week his Majesty dismissed his Prot: Chaplains at Windsor from attending at ye Ceremony of Healing, which was performed by his Romish Priests: ye service in Latin, as in Hen. 7ths time. I am heartily glad to hear you are well at Rydall. God long continue it. I am Sr Your faithful Served I pray Sr that not anything of ye News above be known to come from me. Letters from France say ye Issue of humours wherewith King is troubled does heal up every 2 months, and then breaks out again. How long he may continue thus is uncertain. I do not yet return your book of ye French Persecution. For Sr Daniel Fleming these at Rydall.

Land. June 5th 86 Sr I have yrs of ye 7. 12 & 28th of May. Consequently ye Money for ye Barometer, which you needed not have been so expeditious in, but tic ire method; I thank you for ire opinion abt ye Carrier & am satisfied none but a Kendal carrier can p~form it in 4 days, ye country does not cooperate with me in it, answerable to my good Intentions, & ye Complaint I made abt ye schoolmr of St Bees was not with out cause, after so grt charge & trouble as I had been at, especially when there was no need of it, for had ye Bpp acquainted me, I cld have helped him to a better Mastr than Mr Banks for Apleby, but cannot help St Bees to ye like, being limited to a master born in ye Northern Counties, all I help is to nominate any Body for ye prsent under a Bond of Resignation, for wh I have a blank by me. There is one tho near you, if he answer ye Character I have from Queens & yt he will accept it, may serve us without condition, & yt is one Mr Rich. Jackson who now professes Physic near Kendal, he left Queens abt a year ago, Schollr sufficient, & if no ill habits be since contracted may serve, pray let me have ire thoughts as soon as you can & whether he will accept it if you judge him fit - The Philosophical Collections are I think only seven & fill up ye vacancy betwixt ye 1st 12 vol: of phy: Transactions & those since continued Yrs J.L. For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal Kendal Westmrland

column46: Oxon. June 15 86. Sr Yours of May ye 26th I received, and am very glad to hear that all is well with you. The Bp of Oxon~ has been for a long time so very sick, that his death has been expected daily, and is still so weak that it's thought he cannot possiblely recover. Dr Parrott a member of Parliament for this University died this week. We have a report here of Mr Todd's s inclineing much towards Popery in several sermons which he has lately preached in the country, and yt the Bp has sometimes rebuked him for it. Burnyeat is to be here in the beginning of the next month, and if Mr Brathwaite has not by yt time payed the 20l I would beg of you to lay as much done till he pay it, and send it by Burnyeat. This with my duty to your self and love to all my brothers and sisters. I am Your very dutiful son Hen. Fleming. For Sr Daniel Fleming att Rydal-hall near Kendal These

Sr I have both yrs concerning Mr Richard Jackson & am much obliged to you for them, ye enclosed will show you how much I ought to desire him, & it will be solely his fault if he make not a considerable man. His scholarship I doubt not off, my fears are yt he has something of ye good fellow, & yt he is not stayed & fixed in his temper, I wld willingly lay a foundation yt I might build upon, which makes me so solicitous for a Master, wherein if I mistake my hopes are at an end. I wish he had accepted ye Bond of Resignation, if after he had proved well, it had doubled my kindness, but I esteemed him too much to offer it him, and as a stranger to me I durst not fill ye Place absolutely for fear of being mistaken. So soon as I have enquired a little further I will give him a positive answer, or if he please to go over to Whitehaven according to ye approbation & liking they shall have of him I shall be determined. I see you have no full knowledge of him because you take no notice of an accident abt ye time of his leaving ye College, concerning a Woman, much spoke of in ye Country, but yt is past & sld not weigh, provided he be now but stayed & sober. Ire approbation of ire Barometer has tempted me to send one to Whitehaven. And to ire former enquiry concerning ye Philosophical collections there were never more than seven which you have, but ye Transactions are constantly carried on & now make abt seven or 8 Volumes, being got to I think abt Number 190. I am Sr Ire most humble Served J. Louder. Land. July 6th. 86. My Lt Preston is gon for ye North & will be at ye Assises at Carlisle, pray when you are there learn if you can upon with prtence ye City claims a Toll in Cumberland where they have nothing to doe, it disturbs all or Trade in ye West of Cumberland, & seems a very foolish prtence. My Lt Preston & Sr C Musgrave say they will enquire into it, as being not less concerned for ye County than ye Town. For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydall Kendal Cumberland

Sr By ye paper enclosed in my last, ire recommendation, & a letter this Post from Mr Arch Deacon to ye same purpose, you may easily conclude I have a very good opinion of Mr Jackson, both as to his Natural and Acquired parts, to which if he ad ye application & industry necessary to this Imploymt he may assure himself of al I can do for him: but being so studious as I am of ye advancemt of St Bees, I will not venture on an untried man in that Profession, how promising soever, without a Bond of Resignation, which I now mention more expressly, least I might not sufficiently have explained my self in my last. You know with I design for yt school if ye master prove deserving, & I have offered me other sort of men than Mr Banks was, ready to accept it, were they within or Qualification. The matter of ye School stands thus, Mr Stainton Curate of St Bees, officiates at prsent as Master, but being only put in to prvent a Lapse, is ready to resign, or to let any other execute for a Trial & take al ye Profits, without prtending to anything himself; if therefore Mr Jackson like either of these ways, to go over upon Trial, or to have a new Presentation immediately under a Bond as aboue, he may have his choice, & go over as soon as he please, Mr Tickel will receive him, & put him into Possession of ye School, if he accept it on these terms, but whether he will thus accept it I doubt, from an Expression in yrs, yt there needed no no Bond in his Case, nor need he regard, unless it be his own fault, whether there be or be not, for I know he has Abilities, if he have but Industry & application to yt sort of Imploymt I propose him with al imaginable kindness, & shall ye more make it my Business to advance him, for accepting it on these Terms; I have writ to Mr Tickell to this effect yt he may be ready to receive him if he go, & ye sooner ye better. I beg ire excuse for al this trouble & am Sr Ire most humble served J. Louder Lond~ July 10th 86 For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal Kendal Westmerland.

column46: Rydall, July 16. 86. Sr Yours of ye 6th & 10th instant are come unto my hand; & perceiving your being afraid of Mr Rich. Jackson's being a Good Fellow, I enquired ye other day at Kendall of Mr Mayor, Alderman Simpson, & of some other persons, concerning ye same, who all give a good account of his sobriety, & they think he will be stayed & fixed if he shall meet with due encouragement. As to what you write concerning a Woman I have also enquired after it, & so far as I can discover he appears to be wronged therein. I never moved him much to give a Bond of Resignation; since such Bonds look not (as some think) very well, & by yours of ye 5th of June you did not, as I understood it, expect any from him: But since you insist thereon by your last, he is willing to be bound to you in any thing yt is reasonable, you being his sole Benefactor therein; & as to his entering Bond to any other, he hopes you'll not press him unto it. You intimate as if I knew what Mr Jackson may expect for being School-master of St Bees, which I cannot inform him; having only heard by Report, yt ye Scholmasters certain Salary there is about 24 or 30l~ p~ annum & what you have added to it I do not well remember, if you ever acquainted me therewith. Mr Jackson thinks it necessary yt Mr Stainton first Resign, yt then ye College may present him, & when as he shall have a Presentation, then he must procure a Licence from ye Bishop or Ordinary, & take ye Oaths & make ye Subscriptions, & do what else is appointed by ye Statutes of 17. Car. 2. 2, 25. Car. 2. 2. &c Divers of these things are to be done before he can lawfully or safely teach School at St Bees; and as to his Bond, he will enter yt when you please, if you continue to insist thereon. The Sooner these things are dispatched ye Better, & Mr Jackson hath as great a desire to be at St Bees, as you need wish: But none can fairly advise him to make more hast thither than good speed. He is willing to make you ye sole Judge of his future actions; you being his Friend, & a Person of Honour & Knowledge; & he hopes to be able to perform what you shall expect from him. At ye next Assises I shall enquire after ye Tolls, & I believe Sr G. F. can give you a good account thereof: for I have heard yt he hath a Copy of ye City's new Charter. I hear there was a suit between Sr Francis Radclife & Carlisle concerning concerning this Shire-Toll, & yt Sr Francis was baffled; but how I am not able to inform you, althought he, or his Council, can very well do it. I am Sr Your most faithful Servant Dan: Fleming. For Sr John Louder Baronet these at his House in Southampton-Square London

Sr That I had a very good opinion of Mr Jackson you might p~ceive by my formr & yt ye Bond of Resignation was not proposed but to show my p~ticular care of ye School. Bonds of this Nature are of no good repute as to ye Church, having been often turned to private profit, but Churchmen themselves have approved of this, as ye only means to support ye School under ye circumstances it is. I am therefore well pleased with Mr Jackson's Compliance, ye Bond is to be given to me, but with hopes never to make use of it: for let him be assured if he doe well, there is nothing in my power I will not doe for him yt I can. I have writ to Oxon~ for a new Blank nomination, which I will im~ediately send to Mr Tickel, who at ye same time will take Mr Staintons resignation who now only prvents ye lapse, & will insert Mr Jacksons Name in ye New One & may then also take ye Bond. I leave it to Mr Jackson when he will begin, but because Mr Stainton is very little of a Schooler, ye School suffers at prsent so if he went forthwith & executed it were best Mr S need not come in ye School afterwds but let him take his own method, - I gave you an acct of both ye Phylos. Collections & Transac: if you have anything to com~and me therein you know I am ready to serve you. As to Carlisle prtended Toll, ye new Charter gives nothing they had not before, nor is it in ye prerogative as ye Att. Gen. owns to give a Toll but where there is Quid pro quo as to support & maintain some Bridge or Highway. Sr G. F. writes me he thinks there prtences cannot extend to corn exported, but says no more. Ye Settlemt hereof is a public service. it can only expose ye Corporation for vainer prtences I never heard of. I am Sr Your most humble Served J. Louder. Land. July 24th 86 For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydall Kendall Westmerland

Sr I have had a lettr from Mr Jackson of whom I have very good hopes, & doubt not but I shall have occasion to thank you for him; I have writ to ye prsent Mastr to resign, which as soon as it is done, Mr Jackson shall have a new Presentation, & Instructions in al things yt relate to his Place. My Lt Preston & Sr Chr. Musgrave both told me when they come to Carlisle they with inquire into ye Business of ye Toll pray give ire assistance therein. The Bpp of London is to appear before ye Ecclesiastical Comrs on Monday next but we hear not his Charge. We have yet no acct of ye taking of Bud, I am Sr Ire humble served J. Louder. Land. Augt 7th 86. For Sr Daniel Fleming at Carlisle Cumberland

column46: Oxon~ November 10. 86 Sr I received of Burnyeat 20£, and according to your order have now sent by him 22 Philosophical transactions , which are all as yet printed fro~ Number 160: And considering ye great price of ym here (which is 20s) besides carriage I cannot understand how they should be dearer in ye country in here. I have also sent Dr Plots History of Staffordshire , which is 1s dearer in sheets in with he promised; which makes a great many subscribers here refuse to receive yir books; not questioning but in a short time to have ym much cheaper then 15.s 06d which is now ye price bound. Mr Todd has been in town about 3 weeks, and gives his service to you. We have nothing of news here; for we still want a Dean of Christ Church Coll. And tho~ there was a report about ye Country, yt one Mr Massey of Merton Coll. was to be Dean, yet now it is very much questioned. So hoping all is well with you, with my duty to your self, and love to all my brothers and sisters, I am Your very dutiful Son Hen. Fleming. For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

column46: Oxon~. November 28 86 Sr I being yesterday at Dr Mills chamber he gave me this enclosed Catalogue to send you; and he also bid me acquaint you in all hast that a Collection of all the ancient English Historians are now a printing in Oxon~, in Folio, and in Latin; whereof one volume is very lately published, and the second now in the press; and the rest will be printed with all speed im~aginable. But how many Volumes there will be is not yet known (tho~ 8 or 10 are expected) and so consequently the price neither. If you will be pleased to have them, the Dr (who is concerned in printing them) will secure one of a sort for you: And he dossiers to know your pleasure as shortly as you can let him, least all ye first volumes should be sold. Mr Todd was adviseing me the other day to leave Oxon~, and live with ye Bishp of Carlisle; but I told him, that I left all to you. This with my duty to your self, and love to all my brothers and sisters. I am Your very dutiful Son Hen. Fleming. For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal-hall near Kendal These

column46: Rydal, Dec. 8. 86. - As to what you write concerning Mr Todds adviseing you to leave Oxford & to live with ye Bishop of C. I do not well understand it: For although I had rather you should live with his Lordship than any other person; yet I know not whether he would be willing thereunto; and so long as Mr Todd shall think fit to continue his Lordships Chaplain, I fancy he will be unwilling to entertain any other; Besides I presume yt my Lord and his Lady intend for London in February next, & how long they may be obliged to stay there cannot yet be known. Give my service and hearty thanks unto Mr Todd; for I am confident he intends you well in this Advice; & when as I shall understand it more fully, I can then better know how to advise you. Having the other day an occasion to look amongst some old Papers, I found ye enclosed exactly as you see it. It is all of my own hand writing & was writ Ao 1654. This you may show unto Mr Todd, & I hope He & you will Philosophise thereon. That I may omit no particular of moment, It was wrote at London, with London Ink bought at Gray's Inn Gate, & hath been ever since kept amongst other papers, not any of which are so marked A copy thereof viz. Writ upon ye backside of ye said Note. John Ambrose was ye last Incumbent & was presented 7 years ago unto ye Rectory of Grasmeer in ye County of Westmerland. The Lords Com~issioners granted ye Great Seal unto one John Wallas (who pretended a lapse when there was none) not a year ago, who outed John Ambrose out of ye aforesaid Rectory.

column46: Rydal Dec. 11. 86. My Lord Having acquainted my son Henry Fleming with your Lordships great kindness unto him & me in being pleased to assure me that you would take care of him & help him to some Ecclesiastical Preferment, and He fearing that your Lordship's Great Affairs and the many Petitioners which you daily have with you may occasion your Lordships forgetting of him at Oxford, although Prebends & other Preferments do daily become void; I presume to intimate ye same unto your Lordship and to desire Sr Christo. Musgrave (my good Friend & kind kinsman) sometimes to do ye like; resolving (although I have 13 children to provide for out of a small Estate, formerly sequestered, Decimated & sold by Rebels) to acquiesce cheerfully in your Lordships good pleasure & to remain always heartily My Lord Your Lordships most humble and most obedient servant D. F. For the Right Honble the Lord High Chancellor of England these at London.

column46: Jan. ye 15: 86 Sr Wee came safe hider. I desire you to send me Dupord upon the psalms being a Greek Book as soune as you can, we begging in it morrow, if you please, the Captens are not chosen as yeat. Sr Mr Simpson besowed upon us eader a payer of Gloves when wee came, and Ms Foward would take nothing for what we had, this Sr is all present from Yours obedient son George Fleming.

column46: Oxon~. Jan. 22. 1686. Sr Yours of Decembr 8. I have received and am not a little concerned at the knavery of the book-binder whom I entrusted about Dr Plot's History of Staffordshire. I have got that cut which you want and will take care to send it with Burnyeat. The paper which you sent enclosed in your last, I let Mr Todd and several well experienced in new philosophy see; and their opinion concerning it is that too much coperas being in the ink that writ it, eat those holes in it, which is no extraordinary, nor unusual thing. Burnyeat being to come hither shortly, I must beg of you to assist Mr Braithwait if he want anything of the 20£ then due, so that I may be sure to receive it then. We have little of news here, except that Mr Massey of Merton Coll~ was instilled Dean of Christ-church Coll~. in Christmas: And that yesterday Mr Finch son to my Lord Winchelsey and Fellow of All Souls Coll~. was made Warden of that Coll~ by his Majesties mandate, in the place of Dr. James very lately deceased. Mr Walker published a book this morning, being Two discourses concerning the Adoration of our B. Saviour in the Holy Eucharist : which we expect will be answered by some Oxford man as shortly as possible. This with my duty to your self, and love to all my brothers and sisters, I am Your very dutiful Son Hen. Fleming. For Sr Daniel Fleming att Rydal-hall near Kendal These

column39: The Flemings in Oxford Being Documents Selected from the Rydal Papers in Illustration of the Lives and Ways of Oxford Men 1650-1700. Vol. II 1680-1690. Ed. by Magrath, John Richard. Oxford Historical Society 62. 1913.
column46: March 14th 1686. Worthy Sr I return you many thanks for your kind Letter by this bearer, and particularly for the copy of that you lately wrote to Sr G. which will (I believe) put him hard to it. Possibly I may hear something ere long of his sense of it, for he has sent me word that he intends to be here sometime this week. I presume you have heard of the loss lately befallen my Lt Preston, for which I am heartily sorry. What you write of ye Parliaments being to sit in April is, I believe, very uncertain as yet, for Sr Jo: Lo: (who was pleased to give us ye honour of a visit here the last week) told me he had then newly received a Letter from Sr John of Whitehaven, acquainting him yt it was believed ye Parlt would be dissolved before that time: but of this you will be better informed when you meet with ye Judges at Lancaster. Sr Chr. M. and his son Philip too, have been called into the closet, and though ye Report has been currant here (ever since ye coming in of the last Wednesday's Post) that Sr Chr. was outed of his place in ye Tower, yet I have cause rather to believe the contrary: for by this last Post which came in on Saturday, Sr Chr: wrote to Bas. F. and gave him an account of Mr H. Savill's being displaced & of Vice-Adm. Herbert's being turned out of all his places , yet said not a word of any such thing done to him; and by another Letter, which Bas. recd by ye same Post from one of Sr Chr: servants, to whom he had wrote to let him know how matters stood with Sr Chr: and Phil: he is assured that all is well yet, and both Father and Son very hearty and cheerful, so that Bas. I perceive gives no credit at all to those other stories: and I am prone to believe yt Sr Chr: (being a person so very useful and serviceable) will not be laid aside in hast, nor (consequently) my Lt Dartmouth, though it is taken for granted they are a pair of Protestant Dissenters. I will here enclose a paper which I recd lately from a good hand, and which I believe you will wonder at. Ye Persons therein mentioned have all along been the heads of ye Presbyterian Faction in the town of Newcastle, men of Estates and Interest. You need not trouble yorself to return it, for I have another Copy of it by me. I am glad to hear your Son Mr William keeps so much at home; hoping that by this time he has shaked off those melancholy thoughts wherewith he seemed to be troubled wn he was last here. My Wife presents her humble service to you, and we do both of us return you our most hearty thanks for favouring us thus long with Mris Alice's good company, which indeed hath been so very acceptable to us, yt I assure you we are both of us troubled to part with her. Pray give our services to Mris Barbara, and ere long we hope to give her Joy; yea and to Mr Daniel too, though you say nothing of that in your Letter. I hear my Godson is still threshing hard at it at Sedbergh: God almighty bless him, and all yours. I am Dear Sr Your most faithful Served T.C. For Sr Daniel Fleming these at Rydall.

column46: Oxon~ March ye 14 1686/7 Sr I have sent you by this bearer Burnyeat Mr Walker's book and answer, as also two other books, which are accounted here to be as good as any which have been lately writ. The answer to Mr Walker's book is supposed to be writ by Mr Wake chaplain to my Lt Preston: And ye Guide of Controversies by Dr Will. Sherlock. Mr Walker is now a printing Luther's life and ye History of ye Reformation . Dr Crosthwaite, Dr Hide Mr Allan Fisher &c give their humble service to you, and thanks for your token. This morning I received a letter fro~ my Brother William concerning Gresmere Church and Parsonage House, with a model of the house he designs to build, which I like very well, if the money will finish it, and adorn the church: But I am afraid that it will fall short unless you be pleased to be assisting in wood. So having no news, with my duty to your self. I am Your most dutiful Son Hen. Fleming. One Mr Fisher, Fellow of our Coll~. comes into ye Country with Burnyeat whom I would desire you to make welcome. For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal-hall near Kendal These

column37: rector of Grasmere 1685, rector of Asby 1694-1728

column46: Oxon~ Apr. 16 1687. Sr Mr Garnet of Kendal and one Fallowfeild of Cokermouth taking Oxford for their way into the Country, I could doe no less then acquaint you with what news this place affords. Mr Walker's book of the English Reformation was published very lately; of which I have secured one for you, and design (if possible) to bind it up with its answer, which we daily expect, and so send it you by ye first opportunity. Last Monday one Mr Farmer (a Papist) brought a Mandate from ye King to be President of St Mary Magdalene Coll~, in the place of Dr Clarke lately deceased; but ye fellows of the Coll~. meeting yesterday, rejected the Kings mandate, and elected one Mr Huff fellow of the same College; but with may be the consequence of it we cannot as yett think. All here are very well. This with my duty to your self and love to all my Brothers and Sisters is all fro~ Your very dutiful son Hen. Fleming For Sr Daniel Fleming att Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

Sr You will excuse this slow return to ire last, when you know I have kept my chamber 40 days without so much as ever stirring into ye next room, & am still weak. I am sorry you did not see Mr Jackson when he was at Kendal, but he does extraordinary well, his scholars double so yt he is almost oppressed with numbers. I believe he is lately married to one of Mr Tickels Daughters, a widow & a good discreet Woman fit for Boarders. ye Bpp of Lincoln has given me some Books for ye School, & I writ to ye Bpp of Carlisle yt I hoped we sld share with Appleby in some of his favours, we are too remote to be Rivals, & I know he has to much goodness not to encourage my endeavours, for a grt pt of with I doe is for ye Founders sake being unwilling a charity of an Arch Bps sld sink, as it wld have done with out my care. pray when you see my Lord know if he recd any such letter of mine for I never had an Answer - I desire also to know with effect of ye late Toleration in ye Counties abt you, we have many meetings here. The two Chief Justices have changed their Courts, Lt C. J. Herbert now in ye Common Pleas & Mr Justice has his Quietus. Magdalen Coll~ in Oxon~ has refused ye Ks Mandamus for one nominated to be head of ye House, & chosen & installed one of their own Election. The ViceChancellr & University of Cambridge appeared on Thursday before ye Ecclesiastical Comrs but adjourned till Wednesday next. The K. of France's Journey to Luxemburg does give some Alarm to those pts but they hope for quiet. I am Sr Ire most humble Served J. Louder. Land. Ap. 23 87 Young Con. Braitwait & his Lady are coming to live at Warcop. The D. of Buckingham dyed this day sennigh in Yorksh. I heartily wish you cld be instrumental with ye Bpp to assist Dr Wilson who is in grt Distress, any small Living to begin with & his Countenance, wld enable me to doe better for him herafter, I will write to my Lord when I am a little better in health. For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydall near Kendall Westmerland

column37: gentry lower: son of Sir Daniel Fleming
column39: The Flemings in Oxford Being Documents Selected from the Rydal Papers in Illustration of the Lives and Ways of Oxford Men 1650-1700. Vol. II 1680-1690. Ed. by Magrath, John Richard. Oxford Historical Society 62. 1913.
column46: April ye 30th 86 Sr I have received your letter & according to your command I shall acquaint you with, as well as I am able or time will permit, Sr as for our tableing it is very well, & better then many others which paye a great deal more, but we have but a little chamber, for that our woollen cloes are often thrown up & down, for therefore wee should have sunthing to put them in, and as for our Master he is very cinde to us, and follows us very closely, & whilst we are at ye School he always employs us with making verses, (whilst others are repeating) who make verses, or in sum other such like thing, and whilst we are from school he is always amongst us, with many suclike, Sr we hope that you will be pleased to send for us before it be long, but seeing that is so long two cent of I am Si I shall beg your pardon for my scribbling, and we both of us desire your blessing, which is all at present from Your very obedient Sun to command George Fleming. For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydall. To be left at Mr James Simpsons-shop in Kendall These.

Sedber, May 17, 1687. Sr These are first to beg your pardon and blessing; and after wards to let you know, accordind to your command, that I am very well satisfied both with my school, and my table - for in the former both my Master, and Usher are very cinde unto me; and the other, I find to my great delight in all particulars infinightly to sirpass my expectations, but it now being but a schort time until I hope I schall have the happiness Sr to se you; I school omit to tell you every sircumstans, then being a better opportunity, in the mean while. I reast Your most obedient son, James Fleming. For Sr Daniel Fleming These

June ye 24th 1687 Ever-Honoured Sr I have a boy in my school who I believe would give you content, and his father coming to town very opportunely, last Wednesday, I acquainted him with ye advantage which his son might have, if you were pleased to admit him into your service; he seemed very inclinable to embrace so fair an opportunity, only desires to know what service you'll pleas to expect from him, besides teaching your children, and what you'll please to allow him for his pains; I am sorry your Sonn's Landlady can take no more; for I should be very glad of further opportunities of showing my readiness to serve you and acknowledging the obligations I am under so to doe, I hope in one half years time room will be made for them, and then to receive them, of whom I will promise to take what care I can; and for my Usher (if they be so young as to fall under his hand) I dare well promise for him too, for, I know, I am now very well furnished in that respect, upon which account I think myself very happy, for much depends upon the grounding of young scholars. I am Honoured Sr Your Worship's most obliged and most obedient Servant Posthumus Wharton This, ffor the worshipful Sr Daniel ffleming Knight, att Rydal

column39: The Flemings in Oxford Being Documents Selected from the Rydal Papers in Illustration of the Lives and Ways of Oxford Men 1650-1700. Vol. II 1680-1690. Ed. by Magrath, John Richard. Oxford Historical Society 62. 1913.
column46: Oxon~ July 28. 1687 Sr I received yours with 5s ok, which shall be drunk by ye fellows as soon as possible. I have now sent you two books writ by some Oxford hand, but his name is yett unknown: one of them is a reply to that peace of Mr Walker's which I sent you before: The other is an answer to a part of his second book entitled Church Government, Part 5. And we daily expect an answer to the remaining part of it. I have also sent you a Copy of an old taxation of the Arch-Diaconary of Richmond, which you writ for: in which Arch-Diaconary their are two taxations in the Manuscript, whereas in the rest (except a very few places in the Diocese of York) there is but one. I consulted Dr Hide (who is our Library keeper) Dr Crosthwaite, and some others about these taxations, and according to their opinions the Nova taxatio was made in An~o 20 Edwardi prime; but when either of them was made for certain is unknown: I have writ in the first page of the Copy all which I can find in the MS relating to the time when they were made. I have likewise sent you Dr Burnett's Travels; a book which is prohibited, and of which whole impressions has been ceased: so that they are not to be met withal. Fellows of Mag~. Coll~ are to appear tomorrow before ye Com~issioners, to justify what they allege against Mr Farmer as reasons why they would not admit him President of the Coll~. And last week the Kg sent a mandate to the same Coll~. to stop all elections till the Com~issioners had made an end of there business. About three weeks since the Com~issioners sent for a Copy of the statutes of this University, but there not being a Copy which can be spared, there is one to be writ out, which will require a great time. This with my duty to your Self, and love to all my Brothers and Sisters, I am Your very dutiful Son Hen. Fleming For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal-hall near Kendal These.

Aug. ye 26th 1687 Honoured Sr I am desired and indeed of myself inclined to petition you in behalf of a young Gentleman, whom I really think very deserving, otherwise I should blush to beg your favour for him. He was my scholar a considerable time, and went from me to St. John's in Comb: so well furnished that he gave his Tutor (as I have all along been informed) good satisfaction, there he continued till he was Graduate, having still made due improvement of his time for that I constantly received such a character of him (both as to his behaviour and industry) as I was very well pleased withal; At the first election after he was capable he stood for a ffellowship, but his Interest not being able to hold up against that of his Antagonist, he fell short of his hopes in that point, though without the least stain to his own person or parts, which the other Candidate (my scholar too, and an ingenious man) did himself acquaint me with; sinc that time he hath been employed in teaching a considerable School in Hertfordshire (if I mistake not) which I hope hath rendered him more fit to undertake the management of that place, and office which he is in pursuit of, and is the errand of this paper - The School of Blenkhow (Sr) whereof (I understand) your worship is a Governor, is not (I hear) yet supplied. my humble Request to you then is that you'll please (if you be not already obliged) to favour this young scholar with your Interest, which if you please to grant I shall be in great hopes of his success, and doubt not but he will acquit himself so in the employ, as becomes him, or can easily be expected from him; I humbly crave your Wp's pardon for the trouble and boldness of this hasty scrible, which the experience of your Goodness, and Encouragement of Learning, and the hopes I have of the young man's deserts, prompted me (though as I said in hast which my blots will testify) to present to you, with hopes of acceptance, which shall be added to the long score of your other favours, and always most gratefully acknowledged, by Honoured Sr Your Wop's most faithful humble served Posthumus Wharton This ffor the worshipful Sr Daniel ffleming att Rydal with care.

Sept: 2d 1687. Honoured Sr The last week I made bold to trouble you with two lines in behalf of a young Gentleman who intended to become a Candidate for Blenkhow school, he hath since been in Cumberland, and there understands that the election will not be till after Martinmas, which is a Term too long for him to stay; And his concerns lying so far remote, he thinks it will be too long a journey for him to undertake upon an uncertainty, and therefore seems to decline all further thoughts of proceeding in this Affair, I must leave him to be guided by his own inclination in the matter, but humbly crave your Wp's pardon for my praesumption in requesting so much trouble from you, which by the instance of some ffriends, and the hopes I had of the young man's deserts I was moved to, who am Honoured Sr Your most obliged humble (Servant) Posthumus Wharton. This ffor the Worshipful Sr Daniel ffleming Knight att Rydal.

column37: rector of Grasmere 1685, rector of Asby 1694-1728

column46: Oxon~ September 17 1687. Sr I had writ ere this to have given you an account of the Kings reception here, but having then a swelling in my right hand, by reason of an accidental scratch with a nail, I could not doe it, and the Gazette having described it so well since that time, I doe not think it worth troubleing you with now. The Dean and Cannons of Christ-Church College are cited to appear before the Lords Com~issioners on ye 6th of next month; and shortly after ye Master and some of ye fellows of University Coll~. are likewise to appear, and carry their Coll~ statutes along with them. About a month ago the King sent a letter to ye Fellows of Magdalene Coll~, to admit ye Bishop of Oxon~ their President, and ye Bp by letter (being in indisposed) desired to be admitted by proxy; to which ye fellows answered, yt the place was full, and so they could obey neither letter. When his Majty came hither, all the Fellows of that Coll~. were ordered to attend him; which accordingly they did: where after the King had told them how uncivilly and undutifully they had dealt with him, in disobeying his letters; he strictly com~anded ym to go im~ediately to their chapel, and admit the Bishop of Oxon~ President; upon which they went directly to their Chapel; and the Senr Fellow proposeing whether they would obey ye King, and elect ye Bishop? They answered in their turns, they were as ready to obey his Majesty in all things that lay in their power, as any of ye rest of his Majesties subjects; but the electing the Bp of Oxon~ being directly contrary to ye Statutes, and to ye positive oaths they had sworn, they could not apprhend it in their power to obey him in this matter: Only one or two at most of the fellows then present were for obeying in this. We have not had any book from Mr Walker's press this long time, but we deli expect something, for it's reported yt he hath 1 or 2 ready for publishing. In your last it seemed to be your pleasure that I should come into ye Country this winter, in which I shall very willingly obey you, therefore I must beg of you to send a horse, if you can conveniently, if not I hope to get one here. However I must desire you to send by Burnyeat 20l~, for to clear battles and other arrears, to buy a gown, cassock and other cloths fit to appear in, besides materials for a journey. I am certain less cannot doe. This with my duty to your self and love to all my brothers and Sisters, I remain Your very dutiful Son Hen. Fleming For Sr Daniel Fleming at Rydal-hall near Kendal These

column37: gentry lower: son of Sir Daniel Fleming

column46: Sedbrigh November. 11th 87. Sr I hope that ye Ovid which you writ for arrived safe att your hands; as for our shows which you though fit to have made hear, I formald and have received paying for them 05s - 08d, Sr I desire you to send for us if you have leisure about the 7th of December that being the day our giving over; I hope you will be pleased to let me know what books you think fitting for me to bring home with me, or what other things, Sr their is hear an use that when any goes away to ye College, that he always treats some of the chief of his School fellows with a little ale and cakes, this I Sr let you know not being my self over desirus of but that I only might know your pleasure theirin, I rest as I ough to doe Your most obedient Sun George Fleming For Sr Daniel Fleming att Rydall To be left att Mr James Simpsons-shopp in Kendall These.

Dec. 7th 1687. Honoured Sr Your Son's diligence I have no reason to complain of, he hath been very observant and industrious since he came to me, but really so much time was lost before, that his care and mine hath not yet so fully retrieved it as to furnish him sufficiently for the University; A little time now would be of great use to him, and very much expedite his future progress; I have frequently observed what influence school-Learning hath upon men's following studies, and where it hath been lacking, seldom have the persons proved so much as even tolerable proficients; I am almost confident that if he were continued a little longer at school neither your Worship nor himself would have occasion to repent it, one half year would now doe him more good than double the time hitherto; your younger son is likewise very careful, which I hope may in due time help him through what difficulties he meets with, what other sons you please to commend to me shall with all due care be regarded, for I shall always (when I have opportunity) lay out my utmost endeavours to serve you, who am Honoured Sr Your most humble Served Posthumus Wharton I have often advised both my own nearest relations and others to continue their sons a twelmonth after they thought of sending them to the University, which they have afterwards acknowledged for a kindness, and some that have refused the advise have found yeir mistake. This for the Worshipful Sr Daniel ffleming att Ridal

column39: The Flemings in Oxford Being Documents Selected from the Rydal Papers in Illustration of the Lives and Ways of Oxford Men 1650-1700. Vol. II 1680-1690. Ed. by Magrath, John Richard. Oxford Historical Society 62. 1913.
column46: March 30th 1688. Worthy Sir I am glad to hear that you are all well at Rydall, and return you many thanks for the favour of Mr Harry's good company, and now of Mris Alice's, whom I must entreat you not to expect so soon as Easter, but that you will give her leave to stay as long as you can spare her; they being as heartily welcome to us here as they can be to any friends they have in ye world. The Parson gave us a very good sermon, only he is a little bashful in ye delivery of it, but that will wear off with a little time and practice. I find he has made good use of his time at ye University; and therefore I think you shall do well, after some little longer stay amongst his Friends (till about Whitsuntide) to give him leave to return again to Oxford, where he will now improve fast, for I have reason to believe he is a hard Student. The Bishop of Oxford is now dead (as you will find by what I have herewth sent you) & great pity it is he dyed not a little sooner. So is Sr Tho: Clayton also, Warden of Merton College. The newsletter which you had from Hutton has in deed a great many remarkables in it, were there any great credit to be given to it, but I find Sr G. himself has no great opinion of it; I am sure I have not, having so often found it extremely fabulous. I have sent you mine of ye same date, (with one or two more) by comparing of which you will know with value to put upon that. My wife gives you her service, and I am ever Sr Your most faithful Served Tho. Carliol. The papers which I have sent you by Mr Daniel contain in them all the news which I have had by the 4 last Posts. For Sr Daniel Fleming these at. Rydall.

May ye last (88). Honoured Sr In my last I gave you my full thoughts concerning your son, that I looked upon it as very convenient and much tending to his advantage that he should continue at school till about Xtmas next, Since that letter one or two scholars are gone to the University (though against my mind) out of his seat, and I partly understand that it is some trouble to him to stay behind: I confess I always heartily desire that my scholars should stay their full time and go in their due order, and then I should not fear but (by God's blessing) to send them competently well qualified; but I sometimes fall short of obtaining my desires, and the consequence is their own loss. Your son hath indeed behaved himself very well since he came to me, and hath made improvement answerable to the time. I only wish that he had come sooner; your own great knowledge is more then sufficient to pass a right judgment upon him to which I humbly submit, and if you think fit to commit him again to me my utmost endeavours shall never be wanting to him nor his brothers, nor to any you shall please to commit to Honoured Sr Your Wops most obedient Saved Posthumus Wharton. This ffor the Worshipful Sr Daniel ffleming Knight att Rydal

July 20th 1688. Ever-Honoured Sr Your youngest Son here hath been indisposed these 2 or 3 days - your other sons acquainting me that it was your command to them that you should be informed by a special messenger if any indisposition befell any of them, I wrote a line or two yesterday to give you notice, but ordering the messenger to call on your son, that he might bring you an account from his own mouth how his sickness dealt with him your son (it seems) was not willing to suffer him to finish his journey but told him he was better and the next day (he hoped) he should be perfectly sound. - This morning I find the meezles are visible upon him, so that I hope the worst (if he keep worm, of which I have given his Landlady a charge) will be soon over - however I thought it convenient in regard of your order to your sons to let you understand the matter, and if you please to direct any thing for him to take your directions shall be followed, otherwise I shall not advise him to any physic, unless it be a gentle purge when ye distemper is over. I am in hast honoured Sr Your most devoted Served Posthumus Wharton. This ffor the Worshipful, Sr Daniel Fleming Knight att Rydal.

Sedbridge, July 24. 88. Honoured Sr I know not How or in what Language or words should I express ye sense of gratitude due to you care and tenderness you have to us and so we have need to be as careful of one of another as we can, and as for James I hope he will be well soon for ye Mesles hath almost left him, but for Dick I cannot Resolve you how he is because he is hardly come to ye hight of ym yet but as soon as I can conveniently sed I will let you hear how he is, for ye caryor comes so seldom to Kendall it's uncertain when I shall get one sent, and for Henry he hath given us Ten shillings to pay for what we lye out, and for Aun Array we will get a bed for his, but she Intends to lye with ye maid because she lies so near him and we will be as careful about them as we can with Gods help so I rest Your most obedien Son Roger Fleming. Sir if you think it fit you may send for Aun Array within tow or three days for j think Dick will be well soon for we do not know certainly whether it is ye Mesles or not because their is very few comt forth yet. For Sr Daniel Fleming These att Rydall.

column37: gentry lower: son of Sir Daniel Fleming

column46: Oxon ye 28th of July 88. Sr We arrived here without any danger or misfortune and before the term was over; I was by my Brother (who in all respects is kinder to me than in any wise I was able to expect, so that I am very happy in having him here with me) entered of St Edmund Hall under the tutorige of the Vice Principal Mr Codrington, who is very sober, civil, diligent, and a laborious man, I have a Lector in Logic from him daily, he is accounted one of the most careful in instructing of his Pupils, Dr Mill ye Principal entered me Commoner, because their are here only Gentlemen Commoners, and Commoners, and by his care I have a very good Chamberfellow, he was one of them who were turned forth of Modlens. I have here sent you a Bill of my Disbursements in our journey. Many were the kindnesses that I received at my departure, of which Sr it is but fitting I should give you an account; my Brother William, my Sister Wilson, my sister Alice, & my sister Tetham each of them gave me 5 shillings; my brother Daniel gave me one, and my sister Mary gave me 2s and 6d. These Sr being all which I have at present to writ, I rest Your obedient Son George Fleming. The Bill of my expenses in our journey. For Sr Daniel Fleming att Rydal Theses
